name: Letitia James
subject: I’m running
disclaimer_text: Paid for by VPP
body:
| Hi there, it’s Tish James, and I want you to hear this directly from me:

**I’m officially running for reelection as New York’s Attorney General.**

[Before I share more, will you become a Founding Donor of my reelection campaign by splitting a donation between the Voter Protection Project and my campaign today?](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/105721?t=6&akid=23405%2E878179%2Eo-FzzS)

Since 2019, I’ve had the honor of serving the people of New York. I’ve taken on the powerful — from big corporations, to the ultra-wealthy, to powerful politicians like Donald Trump — and delivered real results for New Yorkers.

When the Trump administration pushed their dangerous and immoral policies that target our immigrant neighbors, I fought back because protecting all New Yorkers makes us stronger.

When Donald Trump defrauded the people of New York, I took him to court and held him accountable.

And as Trump and extreme Republicans ramp up their attacks on everything we stand for – threatening immigrants’ rights, raising prices for working people, and launching efforts to roll back voting rights – I’m using the full power of the attorney general’s office to fight back.

That’s why it’s no surprise Donald Trump is targeting me. He knows I won’t stop holding him and his administration accountable, and he’s mobilizing the entire weight of the Department of Justice to come after me because of it.

But if there’s one thing I’ve learned, it's that you can never back down from a bully.

**I’m running for reelection, friend, and I need you on my side to keep fighting for the rights of New Yorkers and people all across this country.**

[The road ahead is going to be long and expensive, and I’m grateful to have the Voter Protection Project in this fight with me. Will you split a donation of any amount between the Voter Protection Project and my campaign so we can start this race off strong?](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/105721?t=7&akid=23405%2E878179%2Eo-FzzS) If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your split donation between Letitia James and VPP will go through immediately: | [CONTRIBUTE $10 »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/105722?t=8&akid=23405%2E878179%2Eo-FzzS)

Together, we’ll keep up the fight for justice, progress, and equality.

Thank you,

Tish James
Attorney General of New York

# Thank You Michigan
---
| | Dear Friends and Patriots,

Thank you to every supporter who stood with us — your passion, energy, and dedication have been truly inspiring.
I loved traveling across our great state, meeting so many of you in person, and talking about the issues that matter most: fighting government overreach, ensuring local control, protecting our constitutional rights, restoring election integrity, and defending parental rights.
I remain hopeful and determined that, in the years ahead, we will build a stronger, safer, freer, and more prosperous Michigan for our families and future generations.
I’m grateful for all of you, and I look forward to standing with you again soon. 🇺🇸
Very truly yours,Kevin KijewskiRepublican Candidate for Michigan Attorney General

subject: Why I’m supporting a YES vote on Virginia’s redistricting amendment

body:
Virginia voters have the opportunity to make sure our elections stay in the hands of the people, not politicians.
# [](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/629?refcode=em20260328-398&t=1&akid=398%2E12592%2EczkmVS)
Friends,
Donald Trump has made it clear that he’s willing to bend, break, or bulldoze democratic norms if it helps him cling to power.
Now, with the midterm elections coming up, Virginia voters have the opportunity to make sure elections stay in the hands of the people, not politicians.
**_Critically, the upcoming referendum gives _voters_ the right to decide what comes next._**
I’m supporting a YES vote on Virginia’s redistricting amendment because I believe this will restore fairness in our elections and prevent Donald Trump from locking in power months before November.
[**If you’re on board, I’m asking you to join me in supporting Virginians for Fair Elections. They’re working around the clock to reach voters across the Commonwealth with clear, factual information about what this amendment does and why it matters. Will you contribute whatever amount is meaningful to you today?**](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/41?c0=em_ms_vafe_20260328_2.kxX_Ms&amount=3&refcode=20260328-398&t=2&akid=398%2E12592%2EczkmVS)
**[Donate $3 ››](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/41?c0=em_ms_vafe_20260328_2.kxX_Ms&amount=3&refcode=20260328-398&t=21&akid=398%2E12592%2EczkmVS)**
This election is happening on April 21, not in November.
**That means time is running out for the ballot measure committee to reach voters with important education and information.**
The stakes are incredibly high in 2026, and Virginia voters have a serious responsibility in front of us to consider this redistricting amendment and make our choice about what happens next. Unlike other states around the country pushing redistricting, this decision will be made directly by the people of our Commonwealth.
[************If you’re with me on this** , I hope you’ll consider donating to support Virginians for Fair Elections today. I believe this amendment will safeguard Virginia’s elections ahead of this year’s crucial midterm elections. **](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/41?c0=em_ms_vafe_20260328_2.kxX_Ms&amount=3&refcode=20260328-398&t=22&akid=398%2E12592%2EczkmVS)

Emma here, Secretary Becerra’s campaign manager, sharing some exciting updates from the past few weeks on the campaign trail. Check out our new ad! Earlier this week, Secretary Becerra launched his first ad of the campaign, , as part of a seven-figure ad buy. The ad will run on cable and digital in markets across California, showing voters statewide why he’s the best for the job. Secretary Becerra is a proven fighter with a record of lowering costs and expanding health care access that resonates with California voters fed up with the chaos of the Trump Administration. No candidate in this race can match Xavier Becerra’s experience. While billionaires and special interests boost other campaigns with little to no effect, we are confident that our message, and the Secretary’s record of fighting for California, is going to break through now that voters are starting to focus on this election. New Website Have you seen our new website? Check out to learn more about the Secretary, his priorities, and why he’s running to lead California. Stay tuned for more policy releases coming soon! Upcoming Townhalls As Secretary Becerra continues to travel the state, we’re hosting more townhalls for folks to meet him and get to ask questions. Our next townhalls will be in Salinas and Los Angeles. \- and stay posted for Los Angeles Townhall info to come! Endorsements At last month’s convention, we were proud to win the endorsement of the California Young Democrats. This month, we expanded upon that support winning the endorsements of the California College Democrats and Sacramento Young Democrats. The Secretary was also proud to be endorsed by Assemblymember James Ramos , the first California Native American elected to the state legislature and a fighter for the Inland Empire. Becerra has been endorsed by leaders across the state, including statewide organizations like the California Young Democrats, California College Democrats, Laborers International Union of North America (LiUNA), California Primary Care Association (CPCA), and California Faculty Association (CFA), and elected leaders including Senators Eloise Gómez Reyes, Sabrina Cervantes, Jerry McNerney and Melissa Hurtado, Assemblymember James C. Ramos, Assemblymember and co-chair of the Latino Legislative Caucus Juan Carrillo, former Congressman Tony Cardenas, Congressmembers Salud Carbajal, Gil Cisneros, and Raul Ruiz, Monterey County Supervisors Chris Lopez and Luis Alejo, and Riverside County Supervisor Manuel Perez, and many others. Becerra Around the State The Secretary hosted a Youth Town Hall in Fresno, where he got to answer questions directly from young voters and the next generation he’s fighting for. Secretary Becerra attended the California Association of Realtors Homeownership Gubernatorial Forum, where he discussed his plans to make the California Dream accessible to all. Becerra attended the Equality California Forum, where he highlighted his long-standing support for the LGBTQ+ community. body:

| | | [](http://e.goppresidential.com/rd/9z2z0udsok4j23in5n46oucvbmaejn520o20392v4sg_rp22sh2s8i6epr1ctgeaor4cjh2bs)

Friend, Easter is one of the most meaningful days of the year. And for many of us, it’s also one of the easiest to rush through. If you’ve ever reached Easter Sunday feeling spiritually unprepared or wishing you had spent more time reflecting beforehand, I wanted to share something created with you in mind. It’s meant to be simple, steady, and grounding. Here’s what you’ll find inside:
---
* One full Scripture passage each day
* A short reflection to help you process what you’re reading
* A prayer to help you pause and respond

---
No long readings.
No heavy commitment.
Just a daily rhythm to help you approach Easter with clarity and intention. If you’re looking for a way to engage with Easter more thoughtfully this year, I hope this devotional serves you well. You can download your free copy here: [https://resources.preborn.com/he-is-risen](http://e.goppresidential.com/rd/9z2zbr9ecelpl7jubim46l4oijqp5tm3fn2v7ajs9j0_rp22sh2s8i6epr1ctgeaor4cjh2bs) Wishing you a meaningful Easter season, Denise

body:

| | | | | [](https://6s79z9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001F2TKer7FaQzBq-xpehvFqNvWK4Z7UeV8uFy5BPJxTQE1n8A17kTReC146KqrvJKnpyfIPxNvQ_vJBpmdt4_IP2gIDUgmgo1CWms4UkaBN1vx9prFsh49y_gayVLQPxXJDaSDDKCrwTSkw2CySOxXGG-Gt6299UbbO6j-BczLbRtGgn9bEUD00G9zesxiNv2o1JK96EhdNSDfr8LigZloNag8og8BgRoi&c=0M516nLVB4J7k_O55K4urTm70u737jwn8dMBGnYhy7SQcxCidhxm_Q==&ch=bGN_X9DFHrreMSXRHKq2q7ehfLQdJ5_XrICnY0briejWwkdN7gGaFQ==)
---
Peter,
I need to be frank with you. Politico just reported that Democrats could lose their effort to redistrict in Virginia.
If Democrats don't pick up these Virginia seats, MAGA comes into November with an advantage and pathway to saving their skins and cheating their way out of a colossal midterm loss.
---
| [](https://6s79z9hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001F2TKer7FaQzBq-xpehvFqNvWK4Z7UeV8uFy5BPJxTQE1n8A17kTReC146KqrvJKnpyfIPxNvQ_vJBpmdt4_IP2gIDUgmgo1CWms4UkaBN1vx9prFsh49y_gayVLQPxXJDaSDDKCrwTSkw2CySOxXGG-Gt6299UbbO6j-BczLbRtGgn9bEUD00G9zesxiNv2o1JK96EhdNSBYoAjCp1NlU83-tbipVLTS&c=0M516nLVB4J7k_O55K4urTm70u737jwn8dMBGnYhy7SQcxCidhxm_Q==&ch=bGN_X9DFHrreMSXRHKq2q7ehfLQdJ5_XrICnY0briejWwkdN7gGaFQ==)
---
And if Democrats don't get Virginia's seats they need to come from somewhere else:
Colorado.
Never in a million years did I think that I would be calling for Democrats to gerrymander my home state of Colorado. Partisan gerrymandering was always a them thing, not something that we do.
But then last summer, Trump claimed he's 'entitled' to more Republican seats in Congress, and states got to work to give them to him. It's time for the Democratic party to become ruthless about winning. If we don't, MAGA eats us for lunch and we lose our Democracy.

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. ## Senate, House Clash over DHS Funding
The House of Representatives voted Friday [to approve a short-term bill](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OqzAUhJ_GdI78B5jCxZWu6LLabktk7EM4Kwcj-yRZ3n5FXmHrbzSa-b6u09Vjwu324e_gaMnTBq-agAjKFNe64G2lkDfC7QHV9_YAX_KkhOq40FwNU_SYjsk00S0ACnQDTva96XtrrW5W19q5tbIz8yCjDxCVMrFtl34ORnemiw26s01oNUghrJCXMHgpQpiDbtXcqoEZAREpl8t3xo1WWNKRn1AuId-b5FaivTL9j6mRqdHP4XxwMqbGz5yQMFSmxgqbJ-C7rxUqnzElvjy2yONaOfwE2IljOHmhd5xyOZgeMTL9X2ppOmnl0BQX9xemhLXrmRG3u8f03kF_kvd06jcAAP__K7-Cyg) to fund the entire DHS for eight weeks, sending the measure back to the Senate, where Democrat Minority Leader Chuck Schumer says it is "dead on arrival." The move came after House Speaker Mike Johnson angrily rebuked a plan the Senate had agreed to the night before as a "joke," [a dramatic denunciation of a deal](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkDGOwyAURE9jd0QYG2MXFNuky7ZbWp_PxxARiAAnyu1X3itsORppNO_93LYbhBjS_g0P0s3lLdG7RmqNymZ9dWH3DXNqIR1UQS0fgpI3wcXM-MjEulkI8bNNvdWOSNDYkx6UmpRalmXsvR5WLhEJlZXS2XV05BaUi4QZHEkr-6DPNT6KdeB84cMFVxg4osFRCiPF2k2cbGi5XO45pObJxU9-UblgfvRR-9aetRu_OnHtxBWeJ8BZnaG0gJE6ccWc9kK1suqPZvM7sXv2qebEmj8SMesrswSRHanAiyJZNoGduJqRr4pLhMkYMsYaBFTAScm-aPt8hxhDnVU38f0BIf59av8S-dLiNwAA___p_4jk) that Senate Majority Leader John Thune had negotiated after weeks of effort. Johnson and other Republicans [criticized the deal](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOhCAYhJ8GOzb444oWFNfY7bVXGsAfZcOCgd_d-PYX7xWum8wkX2bm5zE_TIghrd_mhZp8nhN-akQiLPOyVR_WjVxOFNKB1ajhRFPyDAJ6LiSHcV5MiOfcNYv2iICyQd0q1Sk1DINsNi2sstI6K20_it5KaHuPaFvXtQL9XTVBXzQhYWyFGER7c6NphXPWyTvYO4ysE7gEyuX2zCHRhj6e-Y3l5vKriXoj2iuTXwwmBlM691zpihhMF5jBJOSlFYPpqPzax2Da8lGRF9wPG4MzqfLd1Mor5X01O1-2yv2RlpBWbkOM3HjCwgs-0dFlVkyGkL-x1JATg6kpetk_IcZQe8U6sb5MiH8V6V-_vjX8BgAA__9_MI1Q) because it didn't fund ICE and Customs and Border Protection. With the stalemate entering its seventh week, President Trump on Friday directed DHS [to pay Transportation Security Administration (TSA) employees](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGOpDAQheHTmIxWUQaMAwebkM2mGyK3XbRrZTCya2bE7Ve9V5j4SZ_0_j8f24fnzOfrtz_IyV62k75bJhGqW0xt51eSUE7h85OaN8tNvpYNAecedI92i57zvY1ddDsRku7IDcaMxizLorvkAoyDH-cpoiELsyVtLeDTw0wa9G47dm8NNNoBYIHhEawfIIRn0BM-J7RqBIospT7-Fj4l0Z7v8kX1EcrRZZdErqb0L4WrwlUSJc75vSlcUznofUjh6uPBJzepXricCtdpgdHA0Ev9PK4-cqUgrY-p9Ze_e2le4dpVF69vzpnbbNQIr8Pzf7uTH8X6cvgvAAD__6myfUc), saying, _" these circumstances constitute an emergency situation compromising the Nation's security."_
## US Troops Injured in Air Base Attack
Ten [U.S. service members were injured in an attack](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLHOozAQhJ_GdEaLDQEKF9fQ5dor0WKvw-aMHdlOUN7-xL3C34000oy-7899vSMHjo_feJCpPq2RzhKoVsqr24vnx15tipXjmwqO05cwp1WBuknQUs2rQw7ftW-c8USKdEOmG8d-HKdp0s1uYNYbaD2A7cF5O5PrnB8GujnyA3W2YXOtgVZzBzBB19oZO7B2s3pQ26Bm0QM5rim3z8Sx7uTDN30otzYdTTB7ra8i9C-hFqGW8zxbu5WL4uqFWq4o1NKBxIMyW4xFcny-MznJUXLGyBgl1or2r0xRFnw7lsh5w0JCLU027nVyCFxuo-jhcSCH_-f1R8Y-Rv0LAAD__546gPs) on Prince Sultan Air Base in Saudi Arabia on Friday, according to U.S. officials. The attack involved Iranian missiles and drones. Two of the troops were [seriously wounded](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OqzAQhZ8GOkfGPwwULm6TLrfdEg32EGblYGSboLz9in2FLY-OdHS-7-sxPZAjb8__-CJXlzRtdJZItVKewloWfq7Vp63ydlBBGD6EOU1Kql5ILdQ4BeT4mUwb3EKkSLfkOgADMAyDblcnBz3LYJfOyG4OGkfoLShrghopgMGW3bUmtRo7KQfZ3fyInfR-9tqq2aqxMZIC15Rv34m3utISP-lN-ebTq41urXUvjf7XqHuj7rhfAFd1hVzZR2rUnTNu4sQsjiJqTmkv4kzHFiiIgkdgMWMhMRhpljDOPczQe7A9WaMXryXY3lpQbXZhPzlGLj00Rj5fyPH3Rv2Tu7dTPwEAAP__mVyAsQ), one of the officials said. The attack damaged several U.S. refueling aircraft. The U.S. and Iran [each submitted ceasefire terms](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkD3O4yAUAE-DOyJ44L-CYht32XZLC8NzeFkCFuBEvv0qe4WvHmlGmj_39W4pUnr8ti80bc9rwk-N2BqW1Ye60yM0l1OjdGK143ShLXkFAQMXisO8ekvxWnXnzY4IqDo0chz1OE7TpLpgZnRSboje6nnrtd9GPQxq2tXupVfCd2S-NqFglkJMQt7cbKVwbnOqh62HmWmBnlout2em1ALu8cpvLDeXX100obWjMvWLwcJgaQEDxfhlDJYjR3IXg8Xjjqkig6WfRK8lcCo2kU3ctmbdX17t6YlvtiKn9DwLVn5W3krOR2WwdMX440MxUh1GpsXjZel_pGs_uvY28C8AAP__K3uBhA) as the conflict starts its fifth week. **Whatever happened to Route 66?** Once America's "Main Street," Route 66 stretched 2,448 miles from Chicago to Los Angeles, carrying Depression-era migrants, post-war families, and cross-country dreamers through the heart of eight states. The iconic highway opened in 1926 and became synonymous with American adventure. In 1960, it even spawned a TV show called _Route 66_ , featuring two young men cruising from one adventure to another in their Corvette sports car, with a memorable theme song by Nelson Riddle. [You can see an opening credits scene here.](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DFvwyAUBOBfg7dYGLAxA0OlKFWHRGqXjhaB5_hVxETwEuT--iodu3b9TrqT7vM4HR1GXC8ndwVLc5pWqCUCEeQpLGXGy0I-rYTrHYrT4wYup0lwMey43AkzBYdxm1QT7AwgQDZgO62V1uM4ymaxMMzK9Cp4HswstVbgnQMluelV3wvToH22cSlMx_nIu9Yb13Hvz1724twLwxSHgJRy-5VwpQXmuKUH5NanaxPtQnQrTL4wcWDiUGttt3Sn-xme-VMc-YXJw4PJ_XftCE-v76q-MTFELMTk_uMPF3KZpuwCJib3XZNtuFWMEcugmeKXq8P4u03_OuxhxU8AAAD__40KffU) Families posed with the Cadillac Ranch outside Amarillo, Texas, and marveled at Arizona's Wigwam Motel, where you could sleep in a concrete teepee. The neon motel signs of Tucumcari, New Mexico, welcomed weary travelers, while in Oatman, Arizona's wild burros, roamed freely through town. Every few miles brought another hand-painted billboard for Meramec Caverns or a kitschy giant roadside attraction. [Here are some archival photos](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL9ugzAYxJ_GbI7MZ8Bm8NCFLV07Iv_5gK81OLKdRLx9lfQROt6ddKf7fV3nq6VIx_ppdzR1SfOBzxKxVsxz2MpC61Z9OioddyxW6RNtTjMIGLiQHMY5WIrn3DXBLIiAskHTKtUppbWWzWZgcMEJlC60GnuvtHZOa3TtgMI5NzZkXm1CwtgKoUV78aNthffOyx5cDyPrBAaqKV--Ex11wyWe6YH54tPeRLPVeitMfjCYGEylWv_zl71VyoSFwfS6xWCCnm_0dj2n3a5YeE73inwYONXC0eZ48mDP0mQTbk-KkcqgWCfW3VJ8T9Z_cXoY-A0AAP__wLd9bA). But Route 66's glory days ended on June 27, 1985, when it was officially decommissioned. The Interstate Highway System bypassed the slower, winding route, strangling small towns that depended on highway traffic. Businesses shuttered, motels closed, entire communities withered. Today, about 85% of the original road remains drivable. A preservation movement keeps the legend alive--restored diners, vintage motels, nostalgic road-trippers seeking authentic Americana. While no longer on maps, Route 66 endures as America's most famous ghost highway and inspiration for many songs. Let's hit the road to [Nat King Cole's popular hit version of _(Get Your Kicks on) Route 66_.](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGP4yAUBOBfg7tY-OEYXFCcFKVLiuikO12DMDxibomJ4DmW__0qW2677TfSjDR_LuZiY4rL_WofqClks-BWExJhMX6uId5ncnmhuKxYrVQ72pINcBgOXBxgNN7GtJu-8TogAooGdSdlL6VSSjSz5uBRDJ47oUIfxCQlYB-OUz8GhQFcE_W7jQsYO84V71o32o47NzlxhOkII-s5-ki5tP9zXGjGkPb8wtK6_GiSnomelYlfDM4Mztu2tXteaZ3wnb_FkpuZOL-YOK23v-b6T378Js5gSLESE6fbN65kC5lifcxMnLqmaP_cYkqxDpL1_P6wMX1t048Oe2n4DAAA___30n5M) _Did you ever drive Route 66 in its heyday, or more recently? Once America's "Main Street," Route 66 stretched 2,448 miles from Chicago to Los Angeles, carrying Depression-era migrants, post-war families, and cross-country dreamers through the heart of eight states. The iconic highway opened in 1926 and became synonymous with American adventure. In 1960, it even spawned a TV show called Route 66 , featuring two young men cruising from one adventure to another in their Corvette sports car, with a memorable theme song by Nelson Riddle. Families posed with the Cadillac Ranch outside Amarillo, Texas, and marveled at Arizona's Wigwam Motel, where you could sleep in a concrete teepee. The neon motel signs of Tucumcari, New Mexico, welcomed weary travelers, while in Oatman, Arizona's wild burros, roamed freely through town. Every few miles brought another hand-painted billboard for Meramec Caverns or a kitschy giant roadside attraction. . But Route 66's glory days ended on June 27, 1985, when it was officially decommissioned. The Interstate Highway System bypassed the slower, winding route, strangling small towns that depended on highway traffic. Businesses shuttered, motels closed, entire communities withered. Today, about 85% of the original road remains drivable. A preservation movement keeps the legend alive--restored diners, vintage motels, nostalgic road-trippers seeking authentic Americana. Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. ## CPAC Focuses on Trump
The Conservative Political Action Conference wrapped up this weekend in Grapevine, marking the first time in nearly a decade that President Trump skipped the annual gathering of the Republican faithful--though [the multi-day event](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDuunjAUhFdjOiNzeBcu0tDdtCnRwT7-seSXbAcuu4-4W0g3xWhmvvnztX-hdTZ8fqMnWb9N3APdxVGtlHeVUGVSmGy4sNiL_N-i4vXgDgImLnoO667RumcfGi0PodeuIdnN8zAv0MHSnNIgHd18wDoATmqZxt4YIOr1saykNDVWvmGih7XrBIixxW5c-tWMMx4j6GVggyBta8xtPanSNxbjnnhRblX0jZNnramw_heDjcF233cbbjyjp4Qfej0MtheKwZais9WqV2Li9SReY-I-egq1cJOj5_W0hT-EufAXn6sYDGUKirgN_KeewdZkqdNtnbNlmtkgPh6t-9lT_-_FS8K_AAAA__-4jIo8) still revolved around him. The Iran conflict drew the most attention on the conference floor, with most attendees backing Trump's military strikes. Some voices, including former Florida Rep. Matt Gaetz, urged caution against deeper involvement, while Iranian American supporters packed the hall with chants of "Thank you, Trump." [Attorney General Ken Paxton](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u3CAQRp_G7lgB_gEXFGnc3bQprdlhvDsSNhZw7fXbR9wiL5DuSCONzvn-fC1fwIH312_YyJXPGpedrhyoFEoLHoCJEA7eT8h80vadMZ43LFrqUchO6GnxwOFe-ta7p_STaskpY3pjtdK2fbtxnLD33aS8USNYO6BdB48reDRSGtOyq89kpyelpJbDA9Rgu2kdDDwH7W3f9JI8l5ge5U2FPpDXcMeT0gPj1gb3LuXITfer0XOj5-u6Ht-5RtRzo-eKjZ6PGLgwVoRUGANV_NdhGz3XXAFY-ORcsqDtmQBJHPApcReQxQYvyALfkZHEGpP4sRGZdigkqpLAmPZ7b5Pzx8UhcB5N08vXBhx-dMv_jXw6_TcAAP__3t6TQA) emerged as the grassroots favorite in his Senate runoff against incumbent John Cornyn, drawing strong applause as keynote speaker at the Reagan Dinner. A high-profile panel on [Islam and immigration](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2ypCAQhZ8GMyxsddCAYBOzu-mGVgvt2FUgFjA68_Zbzivc7ARfnb9_P_MPsuf9-RcDmfJe47zTlT2VQmm2B9pEFg_eT8x8UnhlG88PzqDgIVUrYZwdsv_MXeXMotzYVGQarTs9QANDtZl2fQygdIP9aAeCZXyoAZTT_eAabbu2YnObqRbGplGg-hqbfmjHtde49OCGTnSKHJeY6rJRoTfm1X_iSam2MVTebKUcWbR_BEwCpuu66i9UEi-vneqYngKmO0PApNpbawHTl5H3QrlEuSba7SY5ewzx2OLCKMMrew4yIfsU0UkbQ-CcOe6UpKMjpiJgqpJxx8Xec35o0alnQPbfZuV3f54G_gcAAP__FZKKvg) also generated attention, with speakers arguing that unchecked immigration from Muslim-majority countries poses a threat to Texas values and national security.
## Transmission Line Project Raises Alarms
Oncor and LCRA Transmission Services are seeking state approval to build a [765-kilovolt transmission line](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2SpCAURp8GM7rwyo8EBJuYzaYbWle8TrOLQgGj02-_Zb_CxF_VqfOdPx_zB4YYjs_fuJNr31uaD7pqpNaozD6jL-Qxh-PEGk7av6pP5wtnEKC5GDjYecUQX7PsVreI1fYdud4YaUboYeyezorN0OBHrzerLRipzEBe4TKSNHLALrgbJgawfS9AqAf2ahzspgwuCtZRMiloDS2VR3tSo2-sW3ylk8rDp72L7tlarmz4xWBiMF3X9fjn6WjnPTOYsLTgIzGY7mcMppg8RgZTLimnSivP6aLCYziI55L-km_cp6OF44sqLxgqcYxY9spvbsHI3xYMJiUE117LRRnNF9gMl1YQRws9XzbQQizSo-674tZ8hRhD1YZJ8bljiG_99rPop4P_AQAA__91z5YD) from Central to West Texas, citing rapid population growth and rising energy demand across more than a dozen counties. Residents and environmental advocates argue the proposed routes would [damage rural land](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGO5CAURE-DM1rwgcYOHGzibDbd0PrGn2nUGBAw9vTtVz17hA1LJT29qj8f6weGGNLnbzxo7t8-r4muFql3qqsr6Co5LCGd2MJJx1dz-XzhCgLuXCgO07pjiK9VD_u8iX2SA83SWm1HkDAOj3lUSipN-m5GQFTaG6-FnyxOVm2jsEOY3zChYJJSgDA3lGZUkzcWNwP7qJkWtIee660_qNM3Nh9f-aR6c_kY4vzovTSmfjFYGCzXdd2ejlI_3zWD5Qw7ZQbLexeDJWaH8V_kvWJqR2gt5MRjSMRLzSU3jLwVrM_Gy1d7bOiePCT-hlaM_EeBwWKE4LARbeCRS68V14SCo5o2bkZzx905bYUc6ryXK8QY2t0yLT4PDPHHvf_f4-cMfwMAAP__H9eU8g) and sensitive waterways like the San Saba River, urging regulators to instead route the line along existing highway corridors. The Public Utility Commission of Texas will make the final call later this year, with the line potentially operational by 2030. Advocates warn that communities beyond Central Texas should take note, as similar infrastructure decisions may soon be headed their way.

body:
Verify now to help us close the gap.

Peter,

This one number could spell disaster for President Trump and the GOP...

name: Justin J. Pearson
subject: The status quo is getting nervous
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Justice Democrats
body:
A new poll shows us trailing by a single point.
#
Peter, I'll cut right to the chase:
**This week, a new poll came out and it shows me within ONE POINT of our corporate PAC-backed opponent.**
**One point is the difference between more of the status quo and the brighter future our People deserve.**
That’s why our campaign set a **$35,000 end of quarter goal** , and we need to hit it if we’re going to keep our People-powered Movement in the fight for a better tomorrow.
**[Can you chip in $5 or more right now to help us close the fundraising and polling gap?](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260329-1-jp.GVjt4B&refcode=em20260329-37607&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=2&akid=37607%2E1203867%2EVNjB7O)**
**[Contribute $5](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260329-1-jp.GVjt4B&refcode=em20260329-37607&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=3&akid=37607%2E1203867%2EVNjB7O)**
Our campaign has made real progress, Peter. We’ve been reaching voters who’ve felt left behind and forgotten. And that’s _exactly_ why the status quo feels so threatened.
Because while working families are trying to survive sky-high costs, while our neighborhoods are asking for attention, care, and **real investment** , while our People are begging for leaders who will _actually show up_ , our rival is still playing the same inside game that’s become all too common from Washington DC.
**Here’s what I know:** Our community _can’t afford_ another term of out-of-touch leadership. And unlike our opponent’s campaign, we’re not funded by corporate PACs or special interests. We’re backed by teachers, caregivers, students, and everyday folks who are tired of being treated like an afterthought.
That’s how we’ll win this race, Peter. Not by hoping the system suddenly grows a conscience. We’ll win by organizing, staying present, and meeting voters where they are. But this work isn’t easy and doesn’t come cheap.
**[Will you put $5 or more behind our Movement today so we can meet our goal and turn our one-point poll into a People-powered victory?](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260329-1-jp.GVjt4B&refcode=em20260329-37607&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=4&akid=37607%2E1203867%2EVNjB7O)**
**[Contribute $5](https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260329-1-jp.GVjt4B&refcode=em20260329-37607&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=5&t=23&akid=37607%2E1203867%2EVNjB7O)**
In Love and Service,
Justin J. Pearson

As the DNC’s Executive Director, it’s my job to guide our party’s long-term strategy.
So, as we look ahead to the midterms, here’s a quick update for you:
Democrats need to flip **four** Republican seats to take control of the Senate this November. That means winning races in states like Texas, North Carolina, Ohio, and Alaska. To take back the House, we need to hold the seats we have and flip at least three more.

subject: I am sick and tired
disclaimer_text: Paid For By Giffords PAC; not authorized by any candidate or candidate's committee
body:
We have a decision to make.
#

[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-q12026.IDrYd1&refcode=em260329-1-expansion&t=1&akid=11344%2E3935704%2E_i1C8D)
---
Hello --
This is Steve Kerr, reaching out about an issue that is near and dear to my heart: _Ending gun violence in America._
I lost my father to gun violence when I was 18 years old. I know the pain people feel when they get that call. I don’t wish that on anyone.
I am sick and tired of our politicians offering their “thoughts and prayers” but doing nothing to actually stop gun violence. There’s so much more we can and need to do to stop this epidemic in our country.
**[Gabby Giffords has helped lead the fight to save lives from gun violence, but she can’t do it alone. Will you make your first contribution of the year to my friends at GIFFORDS before their critical end-of-quarter deadline?**](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-q12026.IDrYd1&refcode=em260329-1-expansion&t=2&akid=11344%2E3935704%2E_i1C8D)
**[DONATE](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-q12026.IDrYd1&refcode=em260329-1-expansion&t=3&akid=11344%2E3935704%2E_i1C8D)**
Give me a minute to explain why your donation to GIFFORDS is so important, especially today.
The amount of lives lost from gun violence is heartbreaking. Every time you see another mass shooting on the news, it should be a reminder that there are tools to help stop this.
80% of people want universal background checks. That alone could save hundreds, if not thousands, of lives every year. But right now, the gun lobby is spending millions to fearmonger and stop that progress from happening.
We have a decision to make: _Are we going to continue to let the gun lobby run us over? Will we continue letting our children go to school terrified every day? Or do we want to actually take action to protect each other?_
That’s what democracy is about. We must demand that our representatives listen to us and fight to save lives. If they don’t, then we need to replace them with leaders who actually give a damn.

Charlotte is the Sole Republican Fighting for Your Values in this Race! | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/ee8f2e14cfce/whoischarlotte-5861871?e=9dd54a4530)

| |
### **Why Charlotte Bergmann for Congress – TN-09**

Dear Peter, I am writing to introduce you to a candidate who represents a serious opportunity for new leadership in Tennessee’s Ninth Congressional District — **Charlotte Bergmann** , candidate for Congress. For decades, the people of Memphis and Shelby County have faced rising crime, economic pressure on working families, and a lack of forward-thinking representation in Washington. Charlotte Bergmann is stepping forward to bring **accountability, safety, and economic opportunity back to the forefront of federal leadership.** Charlotte is running to address three urgent priorities that matter to families, businesses, and communities across the Mid-South.
### **Public Safety & Community Stability**
Memphis continues to face one of the most serious crime challenges in America. Charlotte believes Washington must support local law enforcement with resources, technology, and policy reforms that empower officers while restoring safety in neighborhoods. She supports federal partnerships that strengthen public safety initiatives, protect victims, and ensure communities have the tools necessary to combat violent crime.
### **Economic Affordability & Small Business Growth**
Families and entrepreneurs across the district are feeling the weight of inflation, rising housing costs, and regulatory burdens that make it harder to grow a business. Charlotte supports policies that: • Lower the cost of living for working families
• Strengthen small business growth and job creation
• Encourage investment and economic development in underserved communities
• Protect entrepreneurs and local industries from unnecessary federal overreach Her approach prioritizes **economic mobility, workforce development, and restoring opportunity in Memphis and throughout Tennessee’s Ninth District.**
### **Border Security & Workforce Stability**
The federal government has a responsibility to secure the nation’s borders while ensuring lawful immigration systems that support economic stability. Charlotte supports: • Strong border enforcement and national security measures
• A lawful and orderly immigration process
• Policies that protect American workers and stabilize local economies These issues directly impact jobs, public safety, and community resources across the country.
#### **A Moment for Leadership**
For more than **20 years, Tennessee’s Ninth District has been represented by the same leadership in Washington** , and voters are increasingly looking for new voices willing to confront today’s challenges with fresh solutions. Charlotte Bergmann brings a **results-driven, business-minded perspective** focused on restoring accountability and opportunity.
Your support would help ensure that this campaign has the resources needed to effectively communicate Charlotte’s message across the district and compete in a nationally watched race. We would welcome the opportunity to brief your leadership team further on the campaign strategy and discuss how your organization can partner with us in bringing new leadership to Tennessee’s Ninth Congressional District. Thank you for your consideration and commitment to strengthening America’s future.

Let’s be honest.
If you’re a conservative donor in America, you’re getting hammered with urgent fundraising emails every day.
➡️ One candidate tells you the sky is falling ➡️ Another says democracy will end tomorrow (unless you give him money) ➡️ A third tells you there’s a “ _50,000% match_ ” that expires at midnight
Sigh.
Worse, NONE of them ever explains exactly _how_ your donation will move the needle.
After a while, it all starts to sound like noise.
Here’s the truth:
**Most solicitations are written by _consultants_ and donating to them won’t do a darn thing except make them money.**
Because modern elections come down to one thing and one thing only:
**➡️ Which Party puts more ballots in the box.**
That’s it.
Not slogans. Not TV ads.
**Ballots. Ballots. Ballots.**
Charlie Kirk understood this before anyone else.
In 2024, he deployed **THOUSANDS of ballot-chasers** into key battleground districts to find and engage with conservatives who don’t normally vote.
Men and women who support the GOP but whose ballots normally sit _untouched_..._unopened_..._unreturned_...
**Charlie’s ballot-chasers banked _hundreds of thousands_ of these early votes. Maybe millions.**
And Republicans didn’t just win.
They swept.
[ ](https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D)
Now we’re scaling that winning strategy for 2026.
**[Turning Point PAC is preparing to fund 700 new ballot-chasers to keep pace with the Left’s turnout machine. Will you support us?](https://click.parlermailer.com/?%3D%3D)**
Each ballot-chaser has a clear mission:
➡️ Find unmotivated conservatives and make a plan to bank at least **10 votes every day** in the early voting periods.
**At scale, that locks-in TENS OF THOUSANDS of votes daily and HUNDREDS OF THOUSANDS before Election Day.**
_Those_ are the margins that decide control of Congress.
Good strategy matters... but battles are won and lost because of **logistics**.
If conservative donors are spending their money on anything else — they’re funding motion, not action.

| | Friend, **Today, on National Vietnam War Veterans Day, we join together as a nation to remember and honor the service and sacrifices of the men and women who served during one of the most challenging chapters in our history.** This day is deeply personal to me. My grandfather was a Vietnam War veteran, and I grew up witnessing the resilience of his generation. But I also saw firsthand the hurdles he faced over the years. For so many, including my grandfather, the transition home wasn’t easy. I’ve witnessed the frustration and exhaustion that come with navigating post-military life and the VA’s complex bureaucracy to secure the benefits they earned. It’s my firm belief that after serving our country, no veteran should ever have to fight another battle at home just to access the health care and support they deserve. I view my work in Congress as an extension of my thanks to the veterans who served. **My mission is to ensure that the promises made to our military personnel are kept.** On the Armed Services Committee, I’ve focused on securing funding for mental health services and expanding access to military medical facilities, like Walter Reed, so our veterans can receive the care they have earned. _To our veterans: If you or a fellow veteran needs assistance with the VA or any other federal agency, I am always here to help._ With thanks, Sarah Elfreth

Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth broke barriers in 2024, becoming the youngest woman ever elected to Congress from Maryland. She went to Congress with one thing in mind: delivering for Maryland families on the issues that matter most. Whether it's standing up for federal workers, supporting veterans, protecting the Chesapeake Bay, or tackling the affordability crisis head-on, Sarah is on the front lines, fighting for what is right. And Sarah has delivered on her promises. She has spent her first year in the House advocating for the Third District, successfully passing five bills into law, solving over 1,000 constituent cases, and bringing tens of millions in funding back to her community. It’s my firm belief that after serving our country, no veteran should ever have to fight another battle at home just to access the health care and support they deserve. subject: Can I call on you to help protect fair elections in Virginia?
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Virginians for Fair Elections
body:
# [](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/629?refcode=em20260329-400&t=1&akid=400%2E12592%2EyHNE86)
[](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/41?c0=em_ms_vafe_20260329_1.OiET0A&amount=3&refcode=20260329-400&t=2&akid=400%2E12592%2EyHNE86)
_Photo Credit: Covington & Burling LLP_
Hi, it’s Eric Holder. As the Chairman of the National Democratic Redistricting Committee (NDRC), the fight unfolding in Virginia is something I’m keeping a close eye on. It is absolutely critical that the continuing effort by Trump and MAGA Republicans to unfairly rig the midterm elections through an unprecedented series of mid-decade gerrymanders is met _directly and decisively_.
[**If you already know why Virginia needs to vote YES on Fair Elections by April 21, please make a donation to Virginians For Fair Elections today. Then keep reading about why your help is so important.**](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/41?c0=em_ms_vafe_20260329_1.OiET0A&amount=3&refcode=20260329-400&t=3&akid=400%2E12592%2EyHNE86)
**The threat to our democratic system is grave and extremely urgent.** When Trump tries to redraw maps in the middle of the decade to secure a partisan advantage, he is directly distorting representation and weakening the foundational principle that voters choose their leaders, _not the other way around_.
Protecting our democracy requires action that is serious and meets the moment. **That is why the proposed redistricting amendment in Virginia is so important.**
Virginia lawmakers have chosen a different path and are treating this moment with all the urgency it demands.
Instead of engineering backroom deals, they are pursuing a transparent process that allows voters to weigh in. They are placing trust where it belongs: with the voters.
This approach offers a clear contrast to the illegitimate power grabs engineered in Texas and the anti-democratic efforts now underway in Florida. **At a time when manipulation of the redistricting process is spreading, Virginia has the opportunity to reaffirm a basic truth: fair representation is not a partisan principle. It is an American one.**
Virginians for Fair Elections is leading the effort to ensure voters understand what is at stake. This work includes educating communities, countering misinformation, and building the grassroots infrastructure necessary to secure victory at the ballot box.
_None of this happens without resources._
If you believe that election outcomes should be earned, not engineered, I urge you to support this effort today. Your contribution will help protect transparency, accountability, and the integrity of our democratic process.
[**That’s why I’m personally asking you, please, make a contribution to Virginians for Fair Elections today.**](https://act.virginiansforfairelections.com/go/41?c0=em_ms_vafe_20260329_1.OiET0A&amount=3&refcode=20260329-400&t=4&akid=400%2E12592%2EyHNE86)

Our democracy depends on citizens who are willing to act when it matters most.
Sincerely,
Eric H. Holder, Jr.
Chairman, National Democratic Redistricting Committee
82nd United States Attorney General

subject: I apologize.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Maggie for NH
body:
Team, I know I've been in your inbox a lot lately. I'm genuinely sorry to reach out so much.

_But I'd be doing you a disservice if I didn't tell you the truth:_

We’re up against our biggest public fundraising deadline of this entire election cycle — and what we raise in the next couple of days will directly impact our ability to compete in the states that will decide control of the Senate.

#
Peter —
I would say asking for money is my least favorite part of running for office. But that's not even the full truth. I flat-out hate it.
If there were a way to win a U.S. Senate seat without ever asking people to contribute, I would do it.
But those who broke our democracy did it by spending obscene sums to rig the system. Billionaires and corporate mega-donors buy elections and politicians because they know their investments will lead to even greater profits.
For too long, politicians have fallen in line with this playbook because it's easy. We're told this is just how things work in Washington and to settle for the status quo.
It's not true. Those at the top know that the people, united behind a common cause, are the greatest threat to their power. That is why we have scared them.
But they still believe Texas is for sale. They think they can come in with millions of dollars in dark money, drown us out, and install another puppet politician in the U.S. Senate.
That's why this official FEC deadline is so important. It's the first big test of our movement since we started the general election. This is our chance to demonstrate that we have the people power necessary to win this race.
So I hate to ask you for money, truly, but I am going to because I know that taking back Texas and transforming our politics is worth it:

body:
[ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/30?refcode=&t=1001&akid=1930%2E251025%2E-GI4Ue ]Abdul for US Senate [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/30?refcode=&t=1002&akid=1930%2E251025%2E-GI4Ue ]Abdul for US Senate

ICYMI — Donald Trump’s Department of Justice is trying to shut down
Abdul’s campus rallies at UMich and MSU.

[ A ]A post from @LeoTerrellDOJ: 'Jewish students should not be subject to
constant hate and intimidation on their own campuses! Individuals should
not score political brownie points by platforming antisemites! Where is
the leadership at @UMich and @michiganstateu? Silence is unacceptable!
Federal funding should go to institutions that prioritize education, not
ideological agendas or tolerated hate.'

That alone is outrageous. But here's the part we can't stop thinking
about:

Abdul's primary opponent ran the smear first. Now, the same smear pushed
by Democratic establishment voices... is being used by Trump’s DOJ to
justify silencing our campaign.

We wish we were kidding. But the reality is, when it comes to AIPAC and
Israel, Trump and the Democratic establishment are far too often on the
same side.

They support the same broken status quo.

And when someone like Abdul builds a campaign that challenges it, they all
line up to try and shut us down.

Abdul is the only candidate in this race who has never taken a dime from
corporate PACs and has never asked AIPAC for its support. He has been
unequivocal about the genocide in Gaza and the war in Iran. That makes him
the one candidate they can't buy — and clearly, the one they're most
afraid of.

Peter, whether or

clean_body: Peter, January 6th was 5 years ago... ...but for many J6 prisoners, their nightmare is still ongoing. Despite receiving a pardon from President Trump, these unjustly jailed men and women are still struggling to rebuild their lives after 4 years behind bars. Like Damon Beckley. After four years as a political prisoner, Damon came home to a life that had been completely destroyed. His family's landlord evicted them from their home, forcing his wife and son to live in an apartment with no heat. And Damon's health collapsed in prison after contracting MRSA and later requiring emergency cancer surgery. To make matters worse, Damon, his wife, and their son are now facing eviction and possible homelessness again. Sadly, Damon's story is far too common among J6 prisoners. In just the last 60 days, for help from January 6 families struggling to survive. Unless we can count on your help, we 'll be forced to TURN AWAY some of these desperate families. Like I said, Peter... Damon's story is all too common. We recently received a request from Kirstyn Niemela, who spent months living in a camper in a friend's backyard during the freezing New Hampshire winter. Because of the stigma of being labeled a J6er, she has struggled to find stable employment. Now, with odd jobs having dried up during the winter months, she's at risk of losing the truck she depends on for transportation and work. Then there's Benjamen Burlew, who is now two months behind on his mortgage and electric bill after health issues wiped out the family's savings. If they fall any further behind, they could lose the home their children have lived in for 17 years. Five years ago, Damon, Kirstyn, and Benjamen were no different than you or me. They had steady jobs. Loving families. Homes they were proud of. And they believed in President Trump's vision for this nation. But the Far-Left turned them into political prisoners ... because they couldn 't jail all of us. Now these patriots are trying to rebuild their lives from nothing... and many of them simply can't do it alone. Stand in the Gap is their lifeline. That's why Stand in the Gap exists: to provide emergency financial aid, housing assistance, legal support, and medical help to the men and women who sacrificed everything. But we can only respond to these urgent requests with support from patriots like you, Peter. Your support helps provide: Emergency financial aid to prevent homelessness Legal defense funds for ongoing civil lawsuits Medical support for J6ers suffering lasting health problems Basic living expenses while families rebuild their lives January 6th is NOT ancient history, Peter. For these families, it's a nightmare they're still trying to escape. Without our urgent help, many of them will NOT survive to the next chapter. Stand in the Gap is their LAST lifeline... and that lifeline exists SOLELY because of generous supporters like you. Thanks for your help, and God bless, Shane Jenkins Founder and Executive Director of Stand in the Gap Stand In The Gap is registered as a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization. The iconic tagline on the movie poster for the launch of The Social Network movie was "You don't get to 500 million friends without making a few enemies."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/447d5f65-06a2-4d11-8949-8687cb38074e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This week we got a glimpse of just how many "a few enemies" might be and how much it is going to cost Facebook (now Meta.)
* * *
* * *
### **Help us defeat the mainstream media and promote capitalism and American exceptionalism.**
### **[Support The Capitalist, become a paid subscriber today:](https://substack.com/redirect/447d5f65-06a2-4d11-8949-8687cb38074e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ Subscribe Here](https://substack.com/redirect/447d5f65-06a2-4d11-8949-8687cb38074e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
* * *
Two juries this week delivered a seismic shift that Silicon Valley will feel for years. A New Mexico court **[hit Meta with a $375 million penalty](https://substack.com/redirect/ed868836-5efc-46ba-a249-989266cd5128?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** after finding Facebook had essentially served as a digital hunting ground for child predators, feeding minors into harms way with algorithms that prioritized engagement over safety. **[In Los Angeles, another jury awarded $6 million](https://substack.com/redirect/7b3d4e38-6128-4430-a30a-08950b2fd511?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** --$3 million compensatory, $3 million punitive--against Meta and Google, holding their platforms liable for deliberately engineering addictive experiences targeted at young users.
These sums, while not existential for trillion-dollar giants, herald something far larger: the end of the era where social media companies could claim ignorance while knowingly profiting from harm. Plaintiffs focused not on what users posted, but on how the platforms were built--the recommendation engines, notification loops, and design choices that kept vulnerable eyes glued and predators connected. Juries didn't buy their defense. Section 230, long the get-out-of-jail-free card shielding platforms from liability for third-party content, failed to protect against claims of negligent product design. The "we didn't know" excuse collapsed under evidence of internal company awareness of **what was going on** and **decisions to do nothing about it.**
Meta originally faced a $2.1 billion demand in New Mexico. The $375 million final verdict feels almost trifling when juxtaposed against the **[company's disclosed plan to spend $115-135 billion on capital expenditures in 2026,](https://substack.com/redirect/0314bb26-66ef-4230-99d0-b12be0f8f15a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** the bulk fueling its aggressive AI infrastructure push.
_**Until you run the numbers.**_
At an awarded damages rate of $6 million dollars, that equates to 22,500 successful law suits against Meta to consume the entire high-end AI build-out fund. At $375 million it's just 360 such cases. Shift to the originally pursued $2.1 billion scale and the threshold falls to fewer than 65 verdicts. With 3.07 billion Facebook monthly active users, finding 22,500 winnable cases (just 0.0007% of Facebook's user base)--whether involving exploited minors, cyberbullying suicides, algorithm-amplified public humiliations, or cancel-culture pile-ons--is hardly speculative. Personal-injury firms working on contingency and ambitious state AGs now possess a courtroom-tested stick with which to beat Social Media titans with **and they will absolutely give it a go.**
A business trial lawyer captured the stakes cleanly: the individual verdict is **["manageable... a nothing,"](https://substack.com/redirect/7b3d4e38-6128-4430-a30a-08950b2fd511?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** but **["the systematic risk is absolutely gigantic."](https://substack.com/redirect/7b3d4e38-6128-4430-a30a-08950b2fd511?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Another breakthrough case could spawn a flood of filings, accelerating settlements and citations nationwide.
* * *
* * *
### **Help us defeat the mainstream media and promote capitalism and American exceptionalism.**
### **[Support The Capitalist, become a paid subscriber today:](https://substack.com/redirect/447d5f65-06a2-4d11-8949-8687cb38074e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ Subscribe Here](https://substack.com/redirect/447d5f65-06a2-4d11-8949-8687cb38074e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* * *
* * *
This isn't abstract. Early cases center on the heinous exploitation of minors--highly addictive platforms that captured and held young and impressionable eyes, while predators connected and groomed, all via platforms that executives knew were failing to protect users yet resisted meaningful changes that might dent engagement metrics and the bottom line.
The logic snowballs rapidly from there.
Is Meta responsible when its algorithms boost a video of a teenager's drunken mishap at a wedding, turning a private embarrassment into a career-ending global meme? What about the teen driven to suicide by relentless cyberbullying amplified through targeted feeds? Or the wave of destroyed reputations during cancel culture, where a single post--"marriage is between a man and a woman" or skepticism about COVID masks--triggered algorithmic outrage machines that coordinated minority mobs into professional and personal ruin?
We don't yet know the outer bounds of liability. But in an ecosystem of no-win-no-fee lawyers and aspiring prosecutors eager to make their name, the incentive to test every boundary is a certainty.
Meta and their social media peers will appeal, naturally. Bankruptcy remains wildly improbable; these companies print cash from advertising and the voracious appetite for content show no signs of slowing. Yet the precedent is set. **Juries have validated causation between platform architecture and real-world harm.** The blind eye turned toward known risks--while scaling virality at all costs--now carries consequences that until this week were not priced-in.
Critics will counter that holding platforms accountable risks chilling speech or innovation. That's a fair point in theory. But the builders' own choices invited this: aggressive resistance to safety tweaks, prioritization of time-on-site over human cost, and a culture that treated user vulnerability as an optimization variable rather than a red line. Section 230 in relation to free speech online was never meant as blanket immunity for product decisions that foreseeably endanger children or amplify personal tragedy. When the Sec. 230 defense failed in both New Mexico and Los Angeles, the liability roadmap became clear.
This now resembles the long arc of tobacco litigation more than any fleeting tech scandal. _" Social media harm"_ is about to become this generation's class action lawsuit just as emphysema and COPD was for the cigarette companies in the 90s.
Individual cases will start small, focused on the most sympathetic victims--in these cases, exploited minors. Over time, the incidental details will matter less than the pattern:
_**Knowledge of harm being caused + Deliberately insufficient mitigation + Active profiting from the dysfunction = class action lawsuit.**_
Expect decades of legal warfare--discovery battles exposing internal memos, who knew what, when, class actions aggregating thousands of claims, state AG suits layering on public nuisance theories. The cases so far are drips, the torrent has yet to begin.
Social media's architects deserve credit for connecting billions and building tools that reshaped communications forever. Yet unchecked scale without accountability bred exactly the predators, addictions, and mob dynamics now returning as legal claims. The lesson for the next generation of AI tech wunderkids is clear. Denial or deflection no longer works. The path now is self ownership and responsibility, designs with real guardrails, transparent risk acknowledgment, and acceptance that platforms are not neutral pipes but active shapers of behavior. Because failure to do that will show up as a line item on your balance sheet, and probably sooner rather than later.
Markets may shrug at $6 million or even $375 million today but pension funds and retail investors chasing Meta's AI upside should watch the multiplying suits instead. The starting pistol has been fired. The legal marathon--and the mounting bills--will test whether these platforms can evolve from engagement farms into responsible infrastructure. Or whether vindictive users, armed with precedent, will force the reckoning through the courts.
"The Big One" just happened, Silicon Valley's "immunity era" just cracked. The aftershocks are only just beginning.

| | | **** **** **** Hey, Friend, my name is Josh Turek and I’m the Democrat who’s going to replace Joni Ernst in Iowa’s must-win Senate race. _Can I tell you a story?_ When I launched my campaign for State House in 2022, no one thought I’d be able to win in a district Trump won handily twice. However, Friend, as a Paralympian and former pro athlete, **_I know if there’s a will, there’s a way_**. So, I hit the streets of Council Bluffs and Carter Lake to make my case to voters. **The funny thing about my district is, unlike most of Iowa, this neck of the woods is very hilly. Most houses have 10 or 20 stairs leading up to the front porch.** Still, I spent four months knocking on damn near every door in town. Every time someone answered, they’d ask the same question: “ _How in the world did you get up here to my door?”_ [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqtHtWNDtXR0WReOmqZcCOXOeD5Hv8jrBs2gR4cymg2NP762eOOvHiIFZT4pM11kYG3ULpFFl-PvHmAYtj78MzaUufRxowTJd3-MuHEbobxS9a6VKQcTfU2xgzz5HWD1lIJFH8ajZY17QUioNGiggRDmuwNpWwCSruGNklaYTtFqotzyB4LAIuFlJ2zeM3IZYEBM1eR0rOfcqXkhAE8kWi2hLF2fBX9Gg0LcgdSwBnKYqwSMQDjHv-vZpurYI_ZKQVVaWCM8QFiSEzhwmwkdhX5NlIZ6wEd5N2lYjhRfWy4hYBl-s6lkNhY-v8L4mlaxyAQ/4pc/UjZRBUQYRIi3n5nOZnDcCg/h0/h001.nDAedImAE5_2noaS9vveHsam1YHjRnR8fIMgaLfqHYA) | [SPLIT A DONATION](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqtHtWNDtXR0WReOmqZcCOXOeD5Hv8jrBs2gR4cymg2NPx5mFJIHAN33H-YB5ApqYP-NvDAIYLlt4_tlSy9ZKeTNx7GAesRuMmtfXcpG9V56qbqpbTMjlj8vbRq8EEOi0o1F0A_WZZNIMDkqNsIliIxRrI89ahetVp-86Sr8zTfA6PHLYHcHK4PTjOkgCuolZpGKkOttur74g_99n30WgIqJgTzK78OMaR0yeZ2a9wN0m1UAQD4LXXlicLMMuXJA4KL804Ge5DzrHYXDgWXch1REdt_Wk4By3Byj29OwkW9NHz4bn7z7VVOig4SeBj3uzhE/4pc/UjZRBUQYRIi3n5nOZnDcCg/h1/h001.HSjEObFh0muUNt0nQDCg71YWCOgI-02nh-_c3I3XnBc)

**I told them the truth: I crawled up here, one step at a time.** That’s how important this conversation is to me.
Friend, all that sweat and determination paid off on Election Day, when I won by _six votes._
Then, in 2024, I turned my six-vote victory into a six-_point_ victory.
That grit and grind is how we’re going to win in 2026. I’m currently tied with Joni Ernst’s handpicked replacement Republican Ashley Hinson. But, this race won’t be easy. Iowa is one of the most competitive Senate seats in the country, so we’re going to win this _one step at a time_.
One grassroots donation at a time. One county at a time. One voter at a time.
The first step here is showing grassroots strength ahead of our March 31st FEC fundraising deadline. **With your help, I’ll win this open seat and conquer the steep climb up to Capitol Hill.**

clean_body: | | | ** Hey, Friend, my name is Josh Turek and I’m the Democrat who’s going to replace Joni Ernst in Iowa’s must-win Senate race. Can I tell you a story? When I launched my campaign for State House in 2022, no one thought I’d be able to win in a district Trump won handily twice. However, Friend, as a Paralympian and former pro athlete, I know if there’s a will, there’s a way. So, I hit the streets of Council Bluffs and Carter Lake to make my case to voters. The funny thing about my district is, unlike most of Iowa, this neck of the woods is very hilly. Most houses have 10 or 20 stairs leading up to the front porch. Still, I spent four months knocking on damn near every door in town. Every time someone answered, they’d ask the same question: “ How in the world did you get up here to my door?” | I told them the truth: I crawled up here, one step at a time. That’s how important this conversation is to me. Friend, all that sweat and determination paid off on Election Day, when I won by six votes. Then, in 2024, I turned my six-vote victory into a six-point victory. That grit and grind is how we’re going to win in 2026. I’m currently tied with Joni Ernst’s handpicked replacement Republican Ashley Hinson. But, this race won’t be easy. Iowa is one of the most competitive Senate seats in the country, so we’re going to win this one step at a time. One grassroots donation at a time. One county at a time. One voter at a time. The first step here is showing grassroots strength ahead of our March 31st FEC fundraising deadline. Over a dozen states and the District of Columbia could have their mail voting rules upended by an anti-voter ruling.
And if people don’t know about the new deadline — implemented just months before the midterms — or face postal delays, their ballots could go uncounted.
**This case raises the stakes for our voter education and empowerment efforts.** At Fair Fight, we work around the clock to give voters the latest information about election rules so they can cast their ballots with confidence. And we fight to elect Democracy Champions who protect, not restrict, the freedom to vote.

clean_body: We’re fighting back for the freedom to vote | | | “Trump just voted by a method he calls ‘mail-in cheating’”—The Washington Post This level of hypocrisy from our leaders should be stunning. But it’s exactly what we expect from Donald Trump. News broke on Monday that Trump voted by mail in a special election. That’s his right! And that’s the same method that about 1 in 3 voters picked in 2024. After all, mail voting is secure, it’s reliable, and it makes our elections more accessible to people who otherwise may not be able to cast a ballot. But Trump is also leading a Republican crusade to ban mail voting (he doesn’t have the power to do that). And he’s spreading disinformation to say that his own voting method supposedly harms democracy. He votes by mail, but he doesn’t think you should be able to. Not to mention, on that very same day on Monday, Trump Regime lawyers went in front of the Supreme Court to try to sharply restrict mail voting — in a case that Mother Jones says “could disenfranchise hundreds of thousands of voters.” = If you've saved payment info with ActBlue Express, your donation will process automatically: | = | = ---|--- = | = ---|--- = | = ---|--- In the case before the Supreme Court, the Trump Regime and the Republican National Committee want to stop states from counting mail ballots that are postmarked by Election Day if they arrive within a grace period. Over a dozen states and the District of Columbia could have their mail voting rules upended by an anti-voter ruling. And if people don’t know about the new deadline — implemented just months before the midterms — or face postal delays, their ballots could go uncounted. This case raises the stakes for our voter education and empowerment efforts. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
