Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. | [](https://substack.com/redirect/16845bc4-7dee-4d6a-baf1-bcd6264d9510?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
I spoke at four No Kings rallies across Western Pennsylvania yesterday, and I witnessed something special: at all four, people were designated to measure the crowd size as accurately as possible. You might have thought Trump normalized lying about crowd sizes, which made it all the more striking how earnest and serious of an effort this was. There were drones and spotters and it was clear no one would settle for a rough estimate. They certainly wouldn't lie. It was a subtle but important reminder that the truth still matters.
I started the day in Sewickley and then moved on to Greensburg, a city in Westmoreland County that we won in the 2018 special election even as we lost Westmoreland County overall. We don't always win there, so looking at the crowd size is a great barometer. My own personal estimate was 4,000, a shocking number for a town of that size in a "red" county. The center of town was completely taken over:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/d8151f81-2d97-4287-b42d-15a14d870d64?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
From there I went to Johnstown, an old steel and rail city in Cambria County, which Trump wins by around 40 points. Although the crowd was smaller, it was no less passionate, and I thought these two had the best combination of outfits and signs that I saw yesterday:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ddba8c3a-14d0-483a-8c66-136ee1ba0440?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Last, it was back to my hometown of Mt. Lebanon. They had the biggest crowd I've ever seen in Mt. Lebanon for anything besides sports. Talking to people afterward, they came from all over, and for many of them it was their second No Kings event of the day. While I was speaking, I didn't realize Jesus Himself was watching over me (though I think the message is intended for Trump):
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f1c1c798-b87f-4fbe-9a69-61efcbe0a894?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Text of my remarks below. It was an encouraging day for truth and democracy.
............
1\. 250 years ago, America told a king what kind of country this is. We teach our children the words of the Declaration of Independence, how they mean America is a place where we believe we're all created equal.
2\. Now it's like we're back where we started. We wouldn't have to be out here today if Donald Trump, and JD Vance, and Stephen Miller understood they're no better than us, and there are actual limits to their power.
3\. You know they want you to feel like there's nothing you can do, compared to the power they have. That's how they plan to change America forever. But that plan won't work if we refuse to change. All we really have to do is keep believing WE ARE ALL CREATED EQUAL.
4\. That idea inspired Americans to fight slavery and fascism. Talk about making America great.
5\. To me, Donald Trump just makes America very hard to recognize.
* How's it possible that Alex Pretti and Renee Good were killed exercising their most fundamental rights, and there's no justice?
* How's it possible an American missile that killed those Iranian schoolchildren, and there's no accountability? To be an American means to believe that every one of their lives was worth just as much as the lives of our children. No one gave Pete Hegseth permission to murder people in our name.
6\. And where is Congress?
7\. I haven't seen John Fetterman come out from behind the Fox News cameras for awhile, have you? While I have a message for you John: Your support for this war is a disgrace. The way you talk about killing like it's a game is a disgrace. I know you never served a day in your life, but that's no excuse. Those are other people's kids you're sending into harm's way. They need leaders, not cheerleaders. If you can't do that, step aside.
8\. The young people who are over there right now are risking everything for us. But they signed up to defend America, not the oil markets. They swore their oath to the Constitution, not Donald Trump.
9\. Under the Constitution, Congress needs to do it job.
* They need to stop being afraid to vote.
* They need to start telling the truth.
* They need to listen to us.
10\. We didn't vote for this war. And they've spent over $30 billion of our money already and they want $200 billion more. Amazing how last year there wasn't enough money to fund healthcare, and food assistance?
* If we're spending $230 billion, wouldn't you rather give healthcare back to all the people Trump took it away from?
* Do you know how many clean power plants we could build for $230 billion, how many schools, and hospitals, and houses we could build from the ground up? (Wouldn't that be good for Westmoreland/Cambria County?) (Isn't that better than paying for an illegal and immoral war?)
11\. America never got to make that choice though. Because Trump said he would stop wars, not start them. He would lower prices, not raise them. But he broke those promises in the blink of an eye because democracy doesn't mean anything to him.
12\. But again, all that matters is if it means something us. 250 years later this democracy still belongs to us. It will never be Donald Trump's to take away unless we let go of it. Don't let go. Thank you.

This wasn’t an easy decision. It’s been the honor of my life to serve as United States Senator, and I’ve focused on getting results. I was ranked number one in the Senate for bipartisan bills and number three out of one hundred for getting bills passed into law.
**I like my job in the Senate. But I love Minnesota more than any job.**
Minnesota has been the center of America's heartbreak. But we've also been the center of America's hope and courage. I’m inspired by how our state keeps showing up with compassion and resolve — and I couldn’t be any prouder.

I’m running for every Minnesotan who wants to buy their first home, for every parent who wants a better world for their kids, for everyone who wants more affordable health care, and for every Minnesotan who wants to protect our democracy and the state we love.
**Now is our moment to renew our commitment to the common good. I’m asking you to look up to the North Star and to see that there is a better future before us.**
**[If you’re able, I hope you’ll donate today. Your contribution will be split with Deb Haaland.](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/6446?t=6&akid=8490%2E400544%2E87UYOW)**

Gavin Newsom and the radical left have one goal -- to crush my campaign and silence the "America First " movement in California forever. I am fighting tooth and nail to stay at the top of the polls, but as an underdog, the odds are stacked against me. The local Republican movement is standing firm, but we are facing a billion-dollar liberal network that wants us erased. They are terrified because they know I am the only one who can stop their radical agenda from spreading across the nation. It 's been a brutal race and my team and I are giving it all we've got. But as long as I have your support, we are not backing down. I need the entire nation to join this fight. I need you to show the left that when they attack one of us, the whole country stands up. Thank you, \- Steve Hilton Authorized by Steve Hilton for Governor 2026

Hi Derek, it's Ken.
I wanted to share a quick note after spending yesterday with grassroots activists at the No Kings protest in Minneapolis.
In Minnesota, we’re known for being warm. Not the temperature, but the people. We take care of our neighbors, no matter where they’re from or what they look like. We don’t look away when someone is being targeted or harassed. We don’t abandon each other.
That’s exactly what I saw this weekend.
**The strength of neighbors. The power of community. Tens of thousands of people coming together to support and fight for each other. People with a clear and critical message: No Kings.**
It was a reminder of the stakes of this election — and of how formidable a force we can be when we all come together to fight for what’s right.
I left yesterday’s protest feeling inspired and ready to keep fighting. If you attended one of the many protests across the country, I hope you felt the same way.
Derek, the only way forward is to elect more Democratic leaders who will stand up for our communities. That’s exactly what we’re laser-focused on here at the DNC.
[**That’s why, if this weekend inspired you too, I hope you’ll consider pitching in $7 to the DNC today. | Peter, Nathan Johnson is running to make Texas better by ending the Paxton era of corruption so that the AG's Office serves the people. That's why he's earned a huge range of endorsements, and why even more organizations and individuals are uniting behind Nathan to take on the Republicans in the general election. Here are some from just this week ⬇️

* Nathan is the only candidate in our race to be recognized as a Gun Sense Candidate by Moms Demand Action. As Texas's next AG, he'll continue his work protecting Texas families from the tragedies of gun violence.

* Congresswoman Veronica Escobar shares Senator Johnson's commitment to democratic institutions, civil and political rights, and the rule of law. She knows Nathan is the best choice to be Texas's next AG.

* Dallas County Judge Clay Jenkins has dedicated a lifetime to upholding law and order. Judge Jenkins knows that public trust in our legal system is paramount, and he trusts Nathan to restore the purpose and focus of the OAG.

* Congressman Lloyd Doggett is one of the most trusted voices in Texas public life. He's endorsed Senator Johnson because Texas needs a serious, principled lawyer leading the AG's Office again.

| | | Dear Peter,
---
| On this Palm Sunday, we remember a moment of humility, hope, and courage.
As Jesus entered Jerusalem, He did not come with power or force, but with purpose — grounded in faith and a commitment to serve others.
It’s a powerful reminder of the kind of leadership we should strive for today.
In times of uncertainty, our communities need leaders who are guided by faith, who stand firm in their values, and who are willing to serve — not for recognition, but because it’s the right thing to do.
That’s the kind of leadership I am committed to bringing to Maryland’s 6th District.
As we reflect on this day, I’m grateful for your support, your prayers, and your belief in this campaign.
If you feel called to support our efforts as we approach our March 31st deadline, you can do so here:

Friend, In two days, we’ll celebrate Transgender Day of Visibility, a time to honor and fight for our transgender, non-binary, and intersex neighbors. Before colonialism imposed strict gender norms, trans people held sacred and honored roles in many societies. But in more hostile times, trans people have still led movements for liberation and expanded possibilities for all of us. **Since Trump’s election in November 2024, more than 400,000 trans people have fled from Republican-controlled states for their survival. Trans reporter Erin Reed said this is “among the largest relocations in modern history in the U.S.”** 1 The Lemkin Institute for Genocide Prevention has warned about “a sharp escalation in genocidal language and actions against trans people in the U.S.” including __ “actions towards the erasure of trans existence.”2 If you’re trans or gender non-conforming, please know that you belong here and I’m fighting for you—including by supporting multiple policies in Congress to protect your rights. Allies, we need to fight back at the local, state, and federal levels to defend our trans neighbors and our shared humanity. [**Could you add your name to urge Congress to reject deadly anti-trans policies and pass legislation to save trans people’s lives, such as t****he _Transgender Health Care Access Act,_ the _Trans Bill of Rights,_ and the _Equality Act?_**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38h9nrsCCiMen3CGd5zila9jzJnep0tjRIZRggydvVqTFsLFF5IP3wxBGx5JTh8eKqRBrUyLjdg0qDwOY6UsvHNmOlO3ZmCKKmo6vS8Krz8XOq9v0h9vOEbJ4MJqnYJj7VpvfKDut4y5S-OoxRZalEXsYEYaPHXR1fnngmY1Le8nH6CbdM8Lo4jKSUZUwVJdLjZ8WPMfXNPTdRIG0lVwa2KUkCLyvJ3ov9pbIMjY_oppcARbHrPHW3Op_iN9H340Y1gFefOM5GZI1BH9v8P1HmyTIJ0AYdCq5pRC_bd6Y1ntrWBE58f8PaG5u11zuJBKN4/4pc/A4J3P61hTHew7U0VN69dOQ/h1/h001.grwC05QlP4HutHVEgBM1WiEdOQ73pHYcxSIQ1zXIqLk) | [DEFEND TRANS PEOPLE](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm38h9nrsCCiMen3CGd5zila9jzJnep0tjRIZRggydvVqTFsLFF5IP3wxBGx5JTh8eKqRBrUyLjdg0qDwOY6UsvHNYHQ4yegWLaO_TIrl6g7yt8Nr5RR3GdOBAa1milMCdMinymdAxdH_yLwJq6sw6kMoK8lhoS6FTuIv3_y2u5CoJ_EqBO29wPTPUV0dUu8PJ47p-vKQwG9sthECPwLyk9zgzN_zrn5g9bgLK7ZpFCAAt-QrrKfTTft8LdcvB4Lyo_tUFv29WzEjRJLfL9xgVnmHTKX2ofwKx5_HPzO295CGPSdT34wmzQinw-GnoSY9CVs/4pc/A4J3P61hTHew7U0VN69dOQ/h2/h001.c5BqQG7cc1oEI7vl4mkHZasCrT0PPi_Ts1kYbAN6iWc)

I want to lift up my trans neighbors such as Jeynce Poindexter, a community leader who provides resources for LGBTQ+ people at the Trans Sistas of Color Project and the Ruth Ellis Center. She also pushes for policies to expand statewide protections for trans and queer people.
We also remember beloved Black trans women in and near Detroit whose lives were tragically cut short in recent years due to violence: Tahiry Broom (29), Karmin Wells (25), Christina Hayes (38), Ashia Davis (34), Naomie Skinner (25), Dede Ricks (33), Hayden Davis (28), and Natasha Keianna (37).
We will keep saying their names, and demanding that Black trans women matter and deserve protection!
**We must push back against transphobic hate and create a world where trans people are safe and welcomed as their authentic selves.** We can’t let the fascists who want to divide us succeed—and we can’t let them criminalize trans people’s needs or existence.
As the Lemkin Institute for Genocide Prevention’s latest “red flag alert” explains:
The Trump administration is trying to _“scapegoat trans people for all the ills of American society and has been working to make life as difficult as possible for trans people.”_ And some states have passed “terrifying” legislation that _“encourages the harassment of trans people daring to exist in public by monetarily rewarding those who take part in the harassment.”_
**State and federal governments have intensified anti-trans policies** , attacking trans people’s access to lifesaving healthcare, public bathrooms and locker rooms, passports and drivers’ licenses, data privacy, and more.
My Republican colleagues in the House of Representatives are supporting bills to ban trans and queer books nationwide, and passing bills to block Medicaid funding for young trans people’s medically necessary gender-affirming care as well as to jail doctors and parents who support trans youth in accessing this evidence-based care.
**Fortunately these bills are**** _not_****passing in the U.S. Senate so they won’t be signed into law. Congress has successfully blocked anti-trans policies from getting added to must-pass budget bills, and people are also fighting back in the courts and on the streets.**
A federal judge just ruled in agreement with 19 Attorneys General and a Governor who filed a lawsuit to block the Department of Health and Human Services’ recent attempt to deny medically necessary care for young trans people nationwide.
But that fight isn’t over: The Trump administration will likely appeal, and they regularly defy court orders. For example, trans rights groups secured a federal ruling to block the Bureau of Prisons from denying lifesaving care and forcibly detransitioning trans people in federal prisons. But the agency announced it’s doing this anyway.

Thank you. Together, we will continue to demand dignity and safety for Black trans women and all trans people.
I’ve joined the Equality Caucus in Congress, introduced policies to protect trans people’s rights (like the _Justice For All Act_), co-sponsored related policies, and signed Congressional letters opposing attacks on transgender Americans.
I’ve also fundraised for trans-led groups and secured $1 million through legislation for the Ruth Ellis Center—which provides safe, affordable, identity-affirming housing for Black and brown LGBTQ+ youth in my district.
No matter your gender identity or sexual orientation, I’ll never stop fighting for you.
In solidarity,
Rashida

A federal judge just ruled in agreement with 19 Attorneys General and a Governor who filed a lawsuit to block the Department of Health and Human Services’ recent attempt to deny medically necessary care for young trans people nationwide. But that fight isn’t over: The Trump administration will likely appeal, and they regularly defy court orders. For example, trans rights groups secured a federal ruling to block the Bureau of Prisons from denying lifesaving care and forcibly detransitioning trans people in federal prisons. But the agency announced it’s doing this anyway. Thank you. Together, we will continue to demand dignity and safety for Black trans women and all trans people. I’ve joined the Equality Caucus in Congress, introduced policies to protect trans people’s rights (like the Justice For All Act), co-sponsored related policies, and signed Congressional letters opposing attacks on transgender Americans. I’ve also fundraised for trans-led groups and secured $1 million through legislation for the Ruth Ellis Center—which provides safe, affordable, identity-affirming housing for Black and brown LGBTQ+ youth in my district. No matter your gender identity or sexual orientation, I’ll never stop fighting for you. In solidarity, Rashida P.S. body:
Young Trump voters powered his path back to the White House, and in return, he betrayed them. Now they need a vision for the future they can trust.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260329-1&t=1&akid=3304%2E587540%2EVJ5RQR)
Peter,
I’m not going to bury the lead here.
Our end-of-quarter deadline is only **3** days away, and **[hitting our $100,000 goal before midnight on March 31 is critical.](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/2160?c0=em_ms_lwd_20260329_1_buyers._8sI22&refcode=em20260329-3304&amount=5&t=2&akid=3304%2E587540%2EVJ5RQR)**
Let me tell you why this moment — and this deadline — could shape how the rest of the midterms will play out.
Last week, the _Washington Post_ ran a piece about young people who voted for Trump in 2024. What they found was a growing sense from these voters that they had been misled and left behind. Polls are saying that 70% of Americans aged 18 to 29 disapprove of Trump’s presidency.
The message is clear: **they’re having buyer's remorse.**
Young voters who catapulted Trump back to the White House are furious about him waging an endless war in Iran, furious about the devastatingly high prices that never came down, and furious that they were so brazenly lied to.
But here’s the thing. These young voters who feel betrayed by the vision they were sold don’t automatically start showing up for us. They need a reason. They need bold, fearless candidates who can actually relate to what they’re going through. The cost of rent, access to health care, crushing student debt. **They need a vision for the future worth fighting for — and more importantly, one they can trust.**
That’s the work. And the window to do it is right now.
It’s exactly what Leaders We Deserve was built to do. Backing and electing leaders who have the urgency and clarity to meet this moment — people like Claire Valdez in New York, Demi Palecek in Illinois, and Christian Menefee who will go to the mat for working people, and prove this movement can win _anywhere_.
But those victories cost money.
We don’t take a dime from corporate PACs, dark money groups, or special interests, Peter. Our support comes from grassroots supporters like you who believe we can take the Democratic Party in a direction we can be proud of.

I want you to know that I never take your support and confidence for granted. And while the attacks on our work to uphold the values we share keep mounting — and will only continue to do so — your continued support motivates me to never back down from this fight. For the sake of our democracy. Our Constitution. Our future. Donald Trump and his allies will continue to come after me, and anyone else who stands up to him. They hope that their persistent attacks will silence and intimidate others from holding Trump’s corrupt regime accountable. But I’m not backing down. I never have, and I never will. Your support enables me to fight back even harder — not only against the attacks we’ve already faced from Trump and his allies, but against the challenges to come. When I was elected, I understood that I needed to use this extraordinary
opportunity to make a difference in people's lives. And from lowering
prescription drug prices to protecting same-sex marriage through the
Respect for Marriage Act, I’ve worked hard every day since to do just

Time and time again, Wisconsinites have been left behind by the MAGA agenda. Just take a look at the prices at the nearest gas station. **Enough is enough.** Here’s where I need your help: our end-of-quarter fundraising deadline is just around the corner – and we need to reach our fundraising goals to stay on track in our race. From making critical investments like ads – like the ones our opponent already has up and running to attack us! – to making more stops on the trail this spring, we need your help to fight back against the dark money flooding into Wisconsin. Our GOP opponent, Tom Tiffany, already has more than $2 million in the bank – and it’s only going to grow more now that he has Donald Trump’s official endorsement. That’s why analysts are calling this a toss-up race. **[I know that with the strength of this grassroots movement, we’ll be able to show what real people power looks like. Here’s the deal, friend —
I know I’ve sent a ton of these emails. I’m sorry. But this one is different **because Mallory is different, and I’m going to tell you why.**
**[If you’re already on board with her, and want to skip that part, go ahead and chip in now before her end-of-quarter deadline on Tuesday.](https://act.mcmorrowformichigan.com/go/1909?t=2&akid=4310%2E898137%2Ep83dzK)**

---
I’ve known my good friend Mallory for a while now. She made waves back in 2022 with a speech seen by millions of people online — and let me tell you something: I’ve been in this business a long time, and that was one of the best political moments I’ve ever seen.
She stood up on the Senate floor, called out the absolute garbage coming from the far-right, and did not flinch. She told the truth. With fire. With heart. _And people listened_.
Hell, I told everyone I’d show that speech as an instruction manual, and I meant it.
**That’s the kind of leadership we need right now.**
So when I tell you Mallory’s a fighter, I damn well mean it. She flipped a Republican state Senate seat that nobody thought was winnable. Then she helped flip the entire chamber for the first time in 40 years.
Mallory is stepping up because Trump and his billionaire boys club are trying to light our democracy on fire. _**And they’d love nothing more than to take back Michigan while they’re at it.**_
**Michigan is going to be a fistfight. It’s the swing state of all swing states.**
National Republicans are gearing up to spend more than EVER to drown us out. If we don’t crush our early fundraising goals, we’ll have to spend the rest of the year playing catch-up to their war chest. We can’t afford that.
If Mallory’s going to fight back — and win — we’ve gotta get these next few months of her campaign the juice to go all the way.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a510f8f2-7df8-4e09-a20b-07df53a4158f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**On Palm Sunday, Christ entered Jerusalem on a donkey. That mattered.**
**He did not arrive on a war horse. He did not come in imperial splendor. He did not demand power through force, fear, or spectacle.**
[ Pledge your support](https://substack..mkh-GJ2oDwRopc-xuAS-NNt0DeH3cYllph-wEUAB7HI?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=192516465)
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=1454853&post_id=192516465&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTkyNTE2NDY1LCJpYXQiOjE3NzQ4MDY4ODUsImV4cCI6MTc3NzM5ODg4NSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTE0NTQ4NTMiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.2vaFszjYBSltTWA5pM_UwPuV7eCWfN9S4t-6fEnLb3I)
_**The donkey was a sign of humility, peace, restraint, and servant leadership. The Donkey is also the symbol of the Democrat party that was on display at yesterday 's "No Kings" rallies through the country.**_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/583c69c7-54f8-4b23-a912-1d338d8e90ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**That is why Palm Sunday should mean something to anyone who says, "No Kings."**
**If you really oppose kings, then you should also oppose arrogance in government. You should oppose leaders who rule by mandate, intimidation, and moral superiority. You should oppose the idea that the people in power always know best, that parents must submit, that patients must comply, and that dissent is something to be crushed instead of heard.**
_**This voice of dissent is growing and has been heard in testimony at the Capitol, yet these voices are being ignored. Politicians represent all citizens, not just those they agree with.**_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9f0f824d-11d9-4c3c-a896-c5a1d6d50dc1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**That is the problem with so much of the modern "No Kings" movement. It uses the language of anti-authoritarianism, but too often without the humility that Palm Sunday represents. The slogan says no kings, but the attitude often says: submit to our views, our priorities, our moral certainty, or be shamed into silence.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1140d853-a61c-4c4b-905b-cc540a408660?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**I attended to raise awareness of a different "no kings" message: no kings in healthcare, no kings in education, no kings over parental rights, and no kings over medical conscience. In Connecticut, we have seen what happens when government grows comfortable with too much power and too little humility. We have a ruling culture that too often acts as though officials and bureaucracies should have the final word over families, medical decisions, and the raising of children.**
_**What struck me most was that the counter protesters were peaceful. The anger came more from many of those supporting "No Kings." That irony was hard to ignore. A movement that claims to resist authoritarianism should be able to handle disagreement. It should be able to tolerate discussion. It should not react with hostility when someone applies its own slogan consistently to raise the same themes that buck the foundation of the movement.**_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ebaa938f-1160-4ceb-9afd-420b837c6a85?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**To be fair, a few people did understand the point. A very small number agreed that "No Kings" should also apply in healthcare and education. That mattered as they were willing to stand up and confront those that could have ousted them for such agreement with me and disagreement for the herd. **
_**Even a little agreement is better than none. It showed that some still understand that the principle is bigger than the politics of the moment.**_
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5a9bb92d-e87e-4069-babe-d181d7a85e03?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
_The shocker was the Palestinian Flags being distributed to children and using them to pass them out._
**Palm Sunday reminds us that the donkey is not just an animal in a parade. It is a symbol. It is a reminder that true authority is marked by humility. True leadership serves. True strength does not bully; it listens and engages and welcomes an expression of disagreement in search of the common ground for the greater good.**
**So if "No Kings" means anything, it should mean more than opposition to one man, one office, or one political party. It should mean rejecting every form of prideful, coercive rule. It should mean no kings in Washington, no kings in Hartford, no kings in healthcare, and no kings over the family. **
**It should also mean pointing out where our President has done something right for America and not only pointing out the perceived wrongs of his administration. This is why Sen. John Fetterman is such an important voice because he points out where President Trump is acting in the best interests of our nation despite unified opposition by his party.**
**The donkey of Palm Sunday meant humility. If today 's "No Kings" movement has lost that, then it has lost the most important part of the message.**

body:
Trump's "emergency" reasons to take over elections are as fake as his justifications for all these new foreign wars. He's frankly terrified of losing the power he's accumulated and how a real Congress he doesn't control might actually hold him accountable.
We need to make our voices heard now before he ramps things up. Send your letter today and remind our leaders that elections belong to us and not them >> [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/stop-trumps-emergency-plot-to-take-over-elections/?source=direct_link&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-actions]
START WRITING NOW ⇨ [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/stop-trumps-emergency-plot-to-take-over-elections/?source=direct_link&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-actions]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Folks -- Donald Trump’s allies want him to declare a national “emergency,” all so he can take control of our elections .
A draft executive order circulating among MAGA elites would let him federalize election oversight, seize voting machines, and override state and local officials ahead of the 2026 midterms. Under the false banner of “election integrity,” these extremists are laying the groundwork to control how — and whether — our votes are counted.
Congress cannot sit back and wait for this draft to become reality. Lawmakers must move now to block any executive order that would federalize or seize control of our elections and hold immediate hearings to expose this scheme.
Tell Congress: Stop Trump’s emergency power grab. Block any executive order that would federalize or seize control of our elections >> [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/stop-trumps-emergency-plot-to-take-over-elections/?source=direct_link&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-actions]
START WRITING NOW ⇨ [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/stop-trumps-emergency-plot-to-take-over-elections/?source=direct_link&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-actions]
Trump tried to overturn the 2020 election after he lost. Now his movement is pushing him to attempt something even more dangerous: rewriting the rules before ballots are cast.
The backlash has been so fierce that Trump is now denying knowledge of the scheme. But we’ve seen this before. On the campaign trail, he claimed he knew nothing about the extreme Project 2025 agenda. Now that same blueprint is shaping his second term.
If a president can declare an “emergency” to seize election infrastructure, no election in America is safe . That’s why we need Congress to act immediately, before this plot goes any further.
Write your letter now and tell Congress they need to ensure that our elections belong to the people — not to Donald Trump >> [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/stop-trumps-emergency-plot-to-take-over-elections/?source=direct_link&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-actions]

Integrity First Voter Action Project is dedicated to expanding ballot access and increasing voter participation across the country.
Since the Supreme Court gutted key provisions in the Voting Rights Act, extreme politicians have taken advantage to pass harsh laws that restrict access to the ballot box. These restrictions particularly affect disadvantaged communities and people of color. It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

* * *
Peter,
DACA was meant to protect immigrant youth from detention and deportation. But new information confirms what our communities have been experiencing — **261 DACA recipients illegally detained and 86 deported.**
_And that’s only from January to November of 2025._
This latest information is the first admission through government data of the alarming rise in DACA recipients with valid status being targeted and detained by federal immigration agents from ICE and CBP across the country. It also comes while the federal government continues to pressure DACA recipients to self-deport.
**DACA recipients — our coworkers, friends, and classmates — are continuing to be detained and cruelly separated from their families.** Meanwhile, the DACA program continues to be attacked in courts, with efforts in Texas to sever DACA recipients’ access to work permits.
The full breadth of the administration’s refusal to follow the law as it pertains to the DACA program and the deportation protections it enshrines wasn’t known until now.
**We will not stop pressuring lawmakers to deliver permanent protections to the hundreds of thousands of DACA recipients who power our economy and country.**

Peter, DACA was meant to protect immigrant youth from detention and deportation. But new information confirms what our communities have been experiencing — 261 DACA recipients illegally detained and 86 deported. And that’s only from January to November of 2025. This latest information is the first admission through government data of the alarming rise in DACA recipients with valid status being targeted and detained by federal immigration agents from ICE and CBP across the country. It also comes while the federal government continues to pressure DACA recipients to self-deport. DACA recipients — our coworkers, friends, and classmates — are continuing to be detained and cruelly separated from their families. Meanwhile, the DACA program continues to be attacked in courts, with efforts in Texas to sever DACA recipients’ access to work permits. I’m the daughter of two working-class union members. My family immigrated to the United States when I was just 3 years old. While there were challenges along the way, my family built the better life that they were looking for in the U.S.

As I watched my parents make sacrifices in order to provide for our family, I learned the value of a strong work ethic. That work ethic led me to serve in a variety of roles: youth advocate, nonprofit leader, public servant, educator, and engineer.

While I’ve held different titles, my dedication to serving my community has remained unchanged. And I’ve always strived to be worthy of the generosity this country has shown my family and me.

**Right now, our current representation doesn’t understand the challenges that our community is facing. I won’t stand by as extreme Republicans like Ryan Mackenzie and Donald Trump jack up costs for Pennsylvania families while they cut taxes for their billionaire donors.

I’m running for Congress because this district deserves better.**

I will stand up for the district and fight to build an economy where working families like the one I grew up in can afford housing, groceries and utilities, and have a pathway to real prosperity.

| [](https://substack.com/redirect/08986d86-f507-4b55-8b12-0e4152bf4af5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In the late 1990s, Lucent Technologies was America's most widely held stock -- a "picks and shovels" play on the internet revolution. The company lent billions to its own customers so they could buy more Lucent equipment. On paper, revenue soared. In reality, Lucent was financing its own demand. When the customers went bust, Lucent nearly followed. The playbook was simple: manufacture demand through vendor financing, book the revenue, let investors extrapolate, and hope no one notices the circular logic until the music stops.
Today, Nvidia invests $100 billion in OpenAI. OpenAI's CFO acknowledges that "most of the money will go back to Nvidia." Nvidia holds a $3 billion stake in CoreWeave, which has spent roughly $7.5 billion buying Nvidia GPUs -- meaning every dollar Nvidia invested has boomeranged home. Nvidia even agreed to purchase $6.3 billion in cloud services from CoreWeave, effectively guaranteeing it would absorb whatever capacity CoreWeave couldn't sell. When Morgan Stanley mapped the capital flows between just six AI companies, the diagram resembled a plate of spaghetti.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/509f8464-61a2-47c6-8aa5-df4c2fc990e3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
I'm not suggesting the AI revolution is a mirage. But the question of whether a technology is transformative and whether its infrastructure buildout constitutes a bubble are two entirely different questions -- and conflating them is precisely the mistake investors made with fiber optics in 2000, with housing in 2007, and with cryptocurrency in 2021. The internet was transformative. The telecom buildout was still a bubble.
The bubble-spotting framework I developed in my book BOOMBUSTOLOGY uses five independent lenses (microeconomic, macroeconomic, psychological, political, and biological) to evaluate the "bubbly-ness" of an investment dynamic. When multiple lenses converge on the same signal, the probability of a bubble increases dramatically. Disagreement across lenses suggests caution but not alarm. Convergence demands attention. When I apply my five lenses to the current AI infrastructure boom, the convergence is striking.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/59161b54-c0e7-4b68-baad-35bbdf87995f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The first _Boombustology_ lens is **microeconomics** , and focuses on agency problems and incentive misalignment. Here, the signal is unmistakable. Hyperscaler CEOs face an asymmetric payoff: if you spend aggressively on AI and the thesis plays out, you're a visionary. If you don't spend and competitors capture the market, you're unemployed. The fear of missing out (FOMO) leads the proverbial pendulum to swing towards greed instead of fear and is a sure-fire path towards over-investment driven by seemingly rational decision-making
The numbers confirm this pattern. AI-related services generated roughly $25 billion of revenue in 2025 -- approximately 10% of what the hyperscalers spent on infrastructure. Most AI initiatives in big companies have failed to deliver their expected return on investment. Nevertheless, hyperscaler investments are projected to exceed $600 billion in 2026, a 36% increase year-over-year. This level of capital intensity (45-57% of revenues) is usually reserved for utilities and heavy industry, not technology companies.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/43d8fb96-262e-44ee-92c7-1546781ee132?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Perhaps most problematically, however, is the accounting treatment. Current standards give GPU assets 5-6 year useful lives, meaning depreciation is approximately 15-20% per year. Yet actual economic depreciation far exceeds accounting depreciation as industry evidence suggests functional obsolescence in 1-3 years. If depreciation is way understated, as I fear it may be, the reported earnings are overstated and collateral values underpinning billions in debt are more fragile than understood.
My second lens is **macroeconomics** and focuses on credit conditions. Unlike the telecom bubble, the current cycle is not being driven by loose monetary policy -- rates remain relatively elevated. But the scale of capital absorption is beginning to distort credit markets in ways the Federal Reserve is only starting to understand. JPMorgan projects $300 billion annually in AI-related investment-grade bond issuance. The Dallas Fed has flagged that synthetic supply from data center operators' interest-rate swaps may have reached $50 billion in a single quarter.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..Cz6YNmxamVXZtHBKtpBGsPoMWsbGYyB_NC7ij8SAfsI?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=192473883)
And when we put this elevated debt into an industry cycle, we see elevated risk on top of elevated risk. Tech equipment and software investment hit 4.4% of GDP in 2025, approaching dotcom-peak levels. And crucially, the hyperscalers plan to add $2 trillion in AI assets to their balance sheets by 2030, implying $400 billion in annual depreciation expense (if we assume accounting standards don't change). Incidentally, that's more than their combined 2025 profits. This isn't a credit-fueled bubble in the traditional sense, but it is a capital-absorption phenomenon large enough to widen borrowing costs for every other corporate issuer in America, crowding out productive investment elsewhere. And this says nothing about the potential electricity demand shock they're creating that will generate inflation for all American consumers of electricity.
**Lens #3 is psychological** and identifies behavioral biases and herd dynamics. The narrative structure of the AI infrastructure boom is textbook late-cycle: the market debate has shifted from "is AI real?" to "how much bigger will it get?" -- the classic inflection from healthy skepticism to dangerous extrapolation.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/53bf8d4f-9350-4bde-bde0-ff84b373fd1b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Photo by [Mathieu Turle](https://substack.com/redirect/d07fc56f-f863-4d3d-9636-ea13622d7e3a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on [Unsplash](https://substack.com/redirect/5630ca07-8f6f-445b-9600-a943af176007?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Anchoring bias is rampant: Nvidia earning 85% of its revenue from just six customers is seen as evidence of irreplaceable demand rather than dangerous concentration. The "this time is different" rationalizations are sophisticated and partially correct -- which, ironically, is what makes them most dangerous. Bulls correctly note that hyperscaler balance sheets are stronger than Lucent's were. But the strength of the balance sheet at the center of a boom tells you about the system's capacity to sustain excess, not about whether excess exists. Let's not forget that Amazon lost almost all its value in the Dotcom bubble...before going on to become one of the world's most profitable and valuable companies.
My fourth lens is **politics** and reveals a dimension arguably more distortive than anything in the telecom era. The AI buildout has been geopoliticized. Gulf sovereign wealth funds collectively deployed $66 billion into AI and digitalization in 2025, driven not solely by return-on-capital discipline but by Vision 2030 diversification mandates and diplomatic quid pro quos with Washington. Abu Dhabi's ADQ committed $25 billion to U.S. data center power generation during a state visit; Saudi Arabia's PIF struck a $10 billion deal with Google Cloud. When capital allocation is driven by national strategy rather than investment returns, the price signal from that capital is fundamentally distorted. It makes the pool of available financing appear deeper and more durable than market discipline alone would support.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..Cz6YNmxamVXZtHBKtpBGsPoMWsbGYyB_NC7ij8SAfsI?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=192473883)
Add the domestic political dimension -- AI infrastructure has been framed as a national security imperative, making it nearly impossible for any politician to advocate restraint -- and you have a policy environment that systematically disables the brakes. Overinvestment is likely to turn into malinvestment, all of which is driven by easier-than-rational access to capital.
**The biological lens** is the fifth one and asks whether the investment behavior is spreading contagiously through investor populations in a pattern resembling epidemiological transmission. The answer is clearly affirmative. What began as hyperscaler self-funding has infected private equity, private credit, sovereign wealth funds, pension funds, insurance company balance sheets, CMBS and ABS markets, convertible bonds, and leveraged finance -- each new class of entrant validating the thesis for the next. JPMorgan estimates that AI-related debt will touch every corner of the fixed-income market. When the same thesis achieves near-universal penetration across investor types, the "herd immunity" that comes from diversified skepticism has been compromised. In epidemiological terms, we are approaching peak infection rate -- the point where new susceptible hosts are becoming scarce. At some point in the near future, there will be no more incremental sources of capital to pull into the AI infrastructure boom...and that points to a very difficult forthcoming funding dynamic.

#### **So What?**
Five lenses. Four flashing bubble signals, one moderate-to-strong. In my experience studying booms and busts across centuries and asset classes, this degree of cross-lens convergence is rare -- and has consistently preceded significant repricing events.
Does this mean an AI infrastructure collapse is imminent? Not necessarily. The strength of hyperscaler balance sheets -- more than $200 billion in annual free cash flow -- provides staying power that Lucent never had. This bubble, if that's what it is, can persist longer than bears expect. **But the sustainability question isn 't whether Microsoft will go bankrupt. It's whether $300+ billion in annual external financing can be sustained when end-demand revenue remains a fraction of infrastructure spending**. And on that question, the five lenses are unambiguous. Investors would be wise to recall the internet infrastructure boom of the late 1990s.
The fox, who knows many things, recognizes patterns across domains. The hedgehog, who knows one big thing, insists that AI is different. The fox doesn't disagree that the technology is transformative. The fox simply observes that transformative technologies and investment bubbles have coexisted before -- and that the pattern of circular financing, narrative escalation, geopolitical distortion, and cross-market contagion currently visible in AI infrastructure has historically resolved in one direction.
The question is not whether a correction will occur, but what will trigger it -- and whether the securitization of circular cash flows has distributed the risk so widely that the repricing, when it comes, becomes everyone's problem.

Nvidia holds a $3 billion stake in CoreWeave, which has spent roughly $7.5 billion buying Nvidia GPUs -- meaning every dollar Nvidia invested has boomeranged home. Nvidia even agreed to purchase $6.3 billion in cloud services from CoreWeave, effectively guaranteeing it would absorb whatever capacity CoreWeave couldn't sell. When Morgan Stanley mapped the capital flows between just six AI companies, the diagram resembled a plate of spaghetti. I'm not suggesting the AI revolution is a mirage. But the question of whether a technology is transformative and whether its infrastructure buildout constitutes a bubble are two entirely different questions -- and conflating them is precisely the mistake investors made with fiber optics in 2000, with housing in 2007, and with cryptocurrency in 2021. The internet was transformative. The telecom buildout was still a bubble. The bubble-spotting framework I developed in my book BOOMBUSTOLOGY uses five independent lenses (microeconomic, macroeconomic, psychological, political, and biological) to evaluate the "bubbly-ness" of an investment dynamic. When multiple lenses converge on the same signal, the probability of a bubble increases dramatically. Disagreement across lenses suggests caution but not alarm. Convergence demands attention. When I apply my five lenses to the current AI infrastructure boom, the convergence is striking. The first Boombustology lens is microeconomics , and focuses on agency problems and incentive misalignment. Here, the signal is unmistakable. Hyperscaler CEOs face an asymmetric payoff: if you spend aggressively on AI and the thesis plays out, you're a visionary. If you don't spend and competitors capture the market, you're unemployed. AI-related services generated roughly $25 billion of revenue in 2025 -- approximately 10% of what the hyperscalers spent on infrastructure. Tech equipment and software investment hit 4.4% of GDP in 2025, approaching dotcom-peak levels. And crucially, the hyperscalers plan to add $2 trillion in AI assets to their balance sheets by 2030, implying $400 billion in annual depreciation expense (if we assume accounting standards don't change). Incidentally, that's more than their combined 2025 profits. Hello,
This fight is personal to me.
My family has been part of this district for generations, going back to 1893 when my great-grandfather immigrated to Trinidad, Colorado, and built a life here in pursuit of the American Dream.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/2603-q1-ak [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/2603-q1-ak]
I grew up learning my family’s history in Southern Colorado - from my grandfather and uncle’s Kelloff’s Food Markets across the San Luis Valley to my cousin’s Kelloff’s Movie Manor in Monte Vista - I learned what it means to serve a community through small business ownership in rural America.
When you own a small business, you get to know people. You hear what they’re going through. You see how hard folks work just to get by, and how much trust they place in the people who show up for them.
That’s stayed with me my entire life. It led me to help found a number of small businesses. And it’s why I’m running for Congress. I want to give back to the district that has given my family so much.
Right now, we’re coming up on a critical moment for this campaign.
We only have 48 hours left until our FEC filing deadline, and my team is hoping to raise $30,000 by midnight on Tuesday. Can you pitch in $10 or more today to help us reach our end-of-quarter goal? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/2603-q1-ak?refcode=260324-ak-Early-EOQ-Ask&amount=10]

body:
Our most important deadline yet

| |
---
Hi friend, We wanted to reach out because we are officially kicking off our end-of-quarter fundraising push. This is the most important deadline of this campaign so far. Everything we have been doing has been building to this moment. After how close the last election was, we know this race is going to be tough. Our opponents are already preparing to spend heavily to try to defeat Nellie and flip this seat. **MAGA has already invested significantly in flooding the airwaves with false attack ads.** They see this as one of their best opportunities in the country. # [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/128322702/610954405/-1228673924?refcode=em-header&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjQwNyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlMWE5OTA4Yi1hMTJiLWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=XSSwI215-armsKNHhxwB_eEpO2PlICsJFvtQHgJ6T5E=)
This is a different email than I usually send, but it’s important.

Before I pull back the curtain and explain why I decided to run for Congress, will you **[chip in $3](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/128322705/610954413/-1228673924?refcode=em-3.29.26-all&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjQwNyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlMWE5OTA4Yi1hMTJiLWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=XSSwI215-armsKNHhxwB_eEpO2PlICsJFvtQHgJ6T5E=)** today?

**I’m doing this because I believe in the power of community.** As a native of downstate Illinois, I know that our communities thrive when the middle class is strong.

My grandfather was a union painter, and my grandmother was a public school teacher. They inspired my life’s work of championing working families just like mine.
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/128322708/610954419/-1228673924?refcode=em-3.29.26-all&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjQwNyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJlMWE5OTA4Yi1hMTJiLWYxMTEtOWE0OC0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=XSSwI215-armsKNHhxwB_eEpO2PlICsJFvtQHgJ6T5E=)
_Me and my grandma._
From when I hit the campaign trail in 2021, to coming back home from Washington today, I’ve met thousands of folks with similar backgrounds who are struggling to make ends meet with the rising cost of living.

The American Dream has become out of reach for many in Central and Southern Illinois. Before Congress, I fought for workers’ rights and led the effort to raise Illinois’ minimum wage to $15 an hour. I decided to run for this seat to make an even bigger impact in the communities that I love.

I was proud to flip IL-13 from red to blue in 2022 and become the first woman to represent this seat in Congress. We created a strong coalition of working families, farmers, veterans, and more to defeat a self-funded Republican.

body:
It’s about what this job should be.

| | | | |
---
Peter, Earlier this month, Andy Ogles went on a Twitter rant that drew attention across the country. It included inflammatory and hurtful comments, the kind meant to drive division, not solve problems. At a time when families across Middle Tennessee are dealing with rising costs and paychecks stretching thin, that kind of behavior is more than a distraction. It’s embarrassing for our district. And it raises a simple question about his priorities. Because this job isn’t about saying whatever gets attention online. It’s about doing the job the right way — taking issues seriously, treating people with respect, and staying focused on what actually matters to the communities we represent. That’s the decision I’ve made in this race. **To be an adult in the room,** to focus on the work, to keep a level head, and to bring a steady, practical approach to solving problems for Middle Tennessee. We can do better than what we’re seeing right now. As we head toward our first end-of-quarter fundraising deadline, we have an important opportunity to show that there’s real support for a different kind of leadership in TN-5. Hi team,
I'm sure your inbox is full of people running for office asking you for money all the time. But if you've noticed that it really ramps up every three months, here's why.
Every quarter, campaigns like ours have to report our fundraising numbers to the Federal Election Commission (FEC). These numbers are publicly posted, so everyone wants to show how strong their momentum is by reporting a big total.
A lot of campaigns also set quarterly goals to keep them on track for November. We do that here.
So everyone running for federal office is scrambling to close their fundraising gaps and putting a lot of pressure on their teams, and on you, at the same time.
I know it can be a lot. Honestly, I'm grateful that you're even reading this right now. And I promise that I'll never spam you with scammy emails or make up fake deadlines to pressure you into donating.

**When Nancy was 17, she dropped out of high school.** Most kids in that situation fall apart. **But not Nancy.** **I raised her to believe that setbacks don’t define you -__how you rise does.__ ** She grew up hearing the same lessons over and over again: **
👉** Never quit.

clean_body: | | | | | | | | Hi, This is Brigadier General James Emory Mace, U.S. Army (Retired). Today, I write to you not as a soldier... but as a father. I’m a Vietnam War Veteran and Purple Heart Medal recipient. I’ve worn the uniform. I’ve buried friends who never made it home. And I’ve felt the sting of a Nation that sometimes forgets what our sacrifices were for. But my daughter - Congresswoman Nancy Mace - never forgot. Nancy was raised in the shadow of the flag. She saw the uniform. She lived with the deployments. She knew the cost. And instead of running from it, she ran toward it. That’s the kind of person -the kind of fighter \- she is. When Nancy was 17, she dropped out of high school. Most kids in that situation fall apart. But not Nancy. I raised her to believe that setbacks don’t define you -how you rise does. She grew up hearing the same lessons over and over again: 👉 Never quit. 👉 Never run from the truth.👉 And never let anyone tell you thatyou are less than what God made you to be. So I gave her a choice: She picked herself up, took a job at Waffle House, and fought her way back. By 21, she became the first woman to graduate from The Citadel, following in my footsteps. Soon after, she was elected as the first woman to represent South Carolina in the U.S. House of Representatives. She’s been fighting her whole life; for herself, for her kids, for the truth, and now...for her state. Nancy led an evacuation mission in the Middle East after learning a South Carolina family was stranded. Because when your people are stuck in a war zone getting hit with missiles and rockets, the only answer worthy of the office -worthy of our country \- is to get them out. She flew into an active war zone and answered the call when Americans needed help. As a father - and as a Purple Heart Veteran \- I’ve never been more proud of my daughter. That’s why it’s hard when I have to watch Nancy face relentless attacks day after day. Each day that goes out there and fights for you, she’s up against the Establishment’s knife. They stalk her. Send her death threats. She’s even been physically assaulted. But Nancy is my daughter. And I know this: She never backs down. And she never stops fighting. I want to ask you something from one parent, one patriot, to another: Will you support my daughter in the toughest battle of her life? clean_body: Friend, The media wants Americans to believe January 6 is ancient history... ...but for the political prisoners who spent 4 YEARS behind bars , the nightmare didn't end with a presidential pardon. In just the last 60 days, Stand in the Gap has received 10 URGENT REQUESTS for help from J6 patriots and their struggling families... totaling $60,237.28. These are REAL AMERICANS whose lives were SHATTERED by Joe Biden, Nancy Pelosi, and the rest of the Radical Left ... solely for political retribution. I want to highlight each of these requests for you, Friend... ...and I sincerely hope you 'll read each of their stories to the end, because these patriots truly deserve to have their stories heard and understood: Damon B. -- Requesting $10,000 After years as a political prisoner, Damon returned home battling MRSA infections and an autoimmune disease, and facing cancer surgery recovery. His family lost their home while he was imprisoned. Now they face the possibility of homelessness again unless they can finish repairing a small house they bought just to avoid skyrocketing rent. Jesus R. -- Requesting $500 Jesus and his family are struggling just to stay afloat. Their mortgage went up, they're behind on skyrocketing utility bills, and now both of their family vehicles need repairs. In Jesus's own words: " It's just one thing after another." Ethan N. -- Requesting $8,000 President Trump'spardon does NOT protect J6ers from civil lawsuits. Ethan's being sued... despite the fact that he wasn't even in the same city in which he's accused of committing an offense. Stand in the Gap has provided him a lawyer... but he needs help to cover basic expenses while he fights to clear his name. Joseph B. -- Requesting $15,000 Like Ethan, Joseph 's also facing a civil lawsuit... and also like Ethan, he wasn't even in the city at the time the alleged offense occurred. Stand in the Gap has also provided Joseph with a lawyer, but he still needs additional financial help. Peter K. -- Requesting $6,000 Peter is desperate to keep a roof over his family 's head. He needs $3,000 to pay back rent, $1,000 to pay his surging utility bills, and $2,000 to repair the family car. Christian M. -- Requesting $1,000 Christian is in danger of losing his home... and he needs just $1,000 in rent assistance to ensure he's not thrown out onto the streets. Cindy Y. -- Requesting $965 Cindy's trying to clear her name... and while she 's paid for all of her legal expenses out of pocket, she's running out of money. $965 covers the LAST transcript she needs for the appeals court... she's come so far on her own and needs our help to finish her case and clear her name. Kirstyn N. -- Requesting $10,000 Kirstyn has been living in a camper in a friend's backyard in New Hampshire. Because of the stigma of being labeled a J6er, she cannot find stable employment ... and with snowstorms eliminating her ability to work odd jobs, she's in dire financial straits. Worse, she's now at risk of losing the truck she depends on for work and transportation. Benjamen B. -- Requesting $7,180 Benjamen's family is 2 months behind on their mortgage, after critical medical bills and vehicle emergencies. If they fall further behind, they could lose the home their children have lived in for 17 years. They require support to keep their home as their family rebuilds the business they lost after J6. Annie H. -- Requesting $1,592 After January 6, Annie lost her business and her home and became homeless. Worse, she had to fight a 4-year custody battle to get her son back. Companies won't hire her because of the J6 stigma... even rideshare and delivery apps have BANNED her for participating in so-called "domestic terrorism." Now she's fighting just to stay on her feet again. President Trump's pardons gave these patriots their freedom... but that did NOT give them their lives back. They and their families still face devastating consequences because the Far-Left STILL wants to see their lives destroyed beyond repair. We founded Stand in the Gap Foundation because Too often, Stand in the Gap becomes their before homelessness, bankruptcy, or losing everything they've worked for. Right now, to respond to the urgent requests you just read. If we fall short, we WILL have to tell these families that we cannot stand in the gap for them in their time of need. It's a call I don't want to have to make, Friend. Even just a few dollars could mean the difference between paying rent and losing a home... between keeping the lights on and sitting in the dark. Team,

I’m focused on the issues that matter to our state — the ones that affect the day-to-day lives of people across this district.

My campaign isn’t about a personal political agenda. It’s about being a voice for Arizonans who are tired of extremists running our country. Extremists who scream about issues that don’t actually help families.

It’s simple: Arizona families want to be able to see a doctor and fill a prescription without worrying about the cost. They want to buy groceries without stressing about how much the cashier tells them they owe. They want to turn on their AC in the summer without having anxiety about how much the utility bill will cost.

These things shouldn’t be controversial, and they shouldn’t be too much to ask of our government.

But when we don’t have leaders focused on these everyday challenges — when they’re more interested in playing politics than delivering for families — it’s working people who suffer.

I’m running for Congress because I’m ready to get things done and make a real difference in the lives of people across our state. But I can’t do it alone. I need your help. Peter,
The press has noticed one thing about the upcoming April 7 Wisconsin Supreme Court election: the silence.
Outlets are running stories about the lack of stories. Journalists are writing about the silence. And then they move on to the next segment about Iran, the economy, or whatever chaos Trump manufactured before lunch.
The irony is almost funny. Almost.

The stakes of this race could not be higher.
A win on April 7 for Democrats pushes their majority to 5-2 and locks it in through 2030, straight through Trump's presidency and into the 2028 election cycle.
A loss hands MAGA a comeback path, putting them in position to flip the court just months before the 2028 presidential election in one of the most critical swing states in the country.
State Supreme Courts can decide election laws, voting rights, and redistricting in their respective states. If MAGA controls Wisconsin's highest court heading into 2028, the keys to the state are theirs. And they will use them to rig the election.

body:
We’re approaching an important end-of-quarter deadline, and I need your help.

| | | [](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/5298?refcode=jtk474-fr-nat-nd&t=1&akid=8601%2E400544%2Eyltt3y)

Hi, friend, it's Deb Haaland.
My campaign is approaching an important end-of-quarter fundraising deadline in 48 hours, so I wanted to send you a quick note to ask for your help.
[**I’m ready to fight for New Mexico as the next Governor, but I can’t do it without you. I’m running a grassroots campaign powered by your support, and I hope I can count on you once more before midnight.**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/6162?refcode=jtk474-fr-nat-nd&t=2&akid=8601%2E400544%2Eyltt3y)
With New Mexico’s governorship tending to flip parties every eight years, the already crowded Republican field shows they’re coming for this seat, right on schedule. Before long, conservative super PACs and right-wing megadonors will start pouring millions into our state to try to buy a path to victory and take this state backwards.
That’s why I need your help.
If you’re able, can you pitch in to help us cross the finish line? My team tells me we’re just a couple thousand short, and your donation could be the one that puts us over the top. You can use the link below to make your donation:
[**secure.actblue.com/donate/debhaaland_email_1125 &refcode=dpwillis67@gmail.com**](https://act.debhaaland.com/go/6162?refcode=jtk474-fr-nat-nd&t=3&akid=8601%2E400544%2Eyltt3y)
I'm so grateful to have you on my team.

Be fierce,

Deb Haaland

Peter, I know it’s been a difficult time for so many, and it seems like the news cycle is one tragedy after another right now. For those of us who care deeply about our communities, it’s an incredibly tough time. When I worry about the future of our country, or when things look particularly bleak, I try to find solace in faith and prayer, and I always find myself reflecting on a particular passage of scripture from Matthew: _‘For I was hungry and you gave me something to eat, I was thirsty and you gave me something to drink, I was a stranger and you invited me in, I needed clothes and you clothed me, I was sick and you looked after me, I was in prison and you came to visit me.’_ _Then the righteous will answer him, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you something to drink? When did we see you a stranger and invite you in, or needing clothes and clothe you? When did we see you sick or in prison and go to visit you?’_ _The King will reply, ‘Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.’_ While the Trump Administration is stripping Americans of their healthcare, dismantling food assistance, and deploying ICE agents to terrorize our communities, **it is more important than ever that we care for and protect the most vulnerable in our communities.** People’s rights in North Carolina will be on the ballot this November, which is why it’s time for us to come together and flip the House majority. And as long as I have the fire in me to keep fighting for the safety and stability of my district and for Americans nationwide, I will be in service of the “least of these.” **[If you’re with me, please consider pitching in $10 or whatever you can before our end of quarter deadline coming up in a few short days. For those of us who care deeply about our communities, it’s an incredibly tough time. When I worry about the future of our country, or when things look particularly bleak, I try to find solace in faith and prayer, and I always find myself reflecting on a particular passage of scripture from Matthew: ‘For I was hungry and you gave me something to eat, I was thirsty and you gave me something to drink, I was a stranger and you invited me in, I needed clothes and you clothed me, I was sick and you looked after me, I was in prison and you came to visit me.’ Then the righteous will answer him, ‘Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you something to drink? When did we see you a stranger and invite you in, or needing clothes and clothe you? When did we see you sick or in prison and go to visit you?’ The King will reply, ‘Truly I tell you, whatever you did for one of the least of these brothers and sisters of mine, you did for me.’ While the Trump Administration is stripping Americans of their healthcare, dismantling food assistance, and deploying ICE agents to terrorize our communities, it is more important than ever that we care for and protect the most vulnerable in our communities. People’s rights in North Carolina will be on the ballot this November, which is why it’s time for us to come together and flip the House majority. name: Team Gina
subject: This isn’t something we see every day
body:
Whether you live in Amarillo, Brownsville, Houston, Dallas, or a small town in between, we all want the same thing.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
_Wow_. **A packed standing room at our event in Amarillo.**
[****](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260329_2_amarillo.4ywhqv&refcode=em20260329-835&t=1&akid=835%2E299639%2ElXK-c_)
That’s not something we see every day, Peter. People packed the room because Texans are ready for something different — a governor who actually shows up, listens, and fights for them.
And that is exactly what Gina is doing on the campaign trail.
She knows that issues differ all across the big state of Texas, which is why we’re visiting all communities — rural communities and big cities, in red areas and blue ones, because _this campaign is for all of us._
We know the real fight in Texas has never been left versus right. It is the people of this state versus the powerful few who have rigged the system for themselves.
While Texans are working hard, a small group of wealthy insiders and political elites keep calling the shots — raising costs, underfunding public schools, stripping away freedoms, and making life harder for working families.
Gina is running for governor to change that.
She knows Texans are tired of being divided and ignored. And she knows that whether you live in Amarillo, Brownsville, Houston, Dallas, or a small town in between, most people want the same basic things. **Good neighborhood schools, affordable health care, decent jobs, safe communities, and the freedom to make their own decisions.**
That is why this campaign is showing up everywhere, talking to everyone, and building the kind of grassroots power it will take to win. But we’re going to need your help.
**[Will you chip in $5 to help us reach our ambitious $675,000 end-of-quarter fundraising goal to help us travel all across Texas and share Gina’s message?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/625?c0=em_ms_gh_20260329_2_amarillo.4ywhqv&refcode=em20260329-835&amount=5&t=2&akid=835%2E299639%2ElXK-c_)**

Thank you,
Team Gina

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
