Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | | Let me tell you something I learned the hard way. * * *
Trump, the war, gas prices, four-hour airport lines -- it's been a month. Sometimes the only sane response to insanity is to laugh at it. David Shuster counted down his five favorite AI-generated clips of the month, and they hit every nerve: Trump declaring "We won" over a bombed-out Iran, ICE agents reimagined as the Three Stooges bumbling through an airport terminal, and a hip-hop track called "Who Cares What He Says" that might be the most honest political anthem of 2026.
But the top two are something else entirely. An AI Elvis takes the Ed Sullivan stage to sing about gas prices and drone strikes in the style of "Suspicious Minds." And the number one clip -- a YMCA parody that rips through MAGA, Mar-a-Lago, Hegseth, and the whole circus -- is the kind of thing you'll watch twice and then send to everyone you know. This is political satire for the AI age, and Shuster delivers it perfectly.

body:
#

Peter —
You might be wondering how this kid...
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-mar26.8i0KMo&refcode=em260328-1-90&refcode2=4102.734936.iJbxNK&t=1&akid=4102%2E734936%2EiJbxNK)
---
...ended up in the United States Senate, squaring off against Trump and the MAGA Right.
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-mar26.8i0KMo&refcode=em260328-1-90&refcode2=4102.734936.iJbxNK&t=2&akid=4102%2E734936%2EiJbxNK)
---
Let’s go back to the start. Ruben, his mom, and his sisters didn’t have much. It was tough. He grew up sleeping on the floor of their apartment because that’s all they could afford.
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-mar26.8i0KMo&refcode=em260328-1-90&refcode2=4102.734936.iJbxNK&t=3&akid=4102%2E734936%2EiJbxNK)
---
Ruben decided, then and there, that he was going to build a better life for himself and his family. He worked every job you can think of to help make ends meet.
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-mar26.8i0KMo&refcode=em260328-1-90&refcode2=4102.734936.iJbxNK&t=4&akid=4102%2E734936%2EiJbxNK)
---
After a lot of hard work, and a ton of help from his family and community, he got into Harvard. It was a lifelong dream, and he made it. But before he graduated, he joined the Marines to give back to the country that gave him so much.
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-mar26.8i0KMo&refcode=em260328-1-90&refcode2=4102.734936.iJbxNK&t=5&akid=4102%2E734936%2EiJbxNK)
---
He deployed to al Anbar, Iraq with his brothers in arms. They called them “Lucky Lima” at the start of their deployment, but that changed eventually. Ruben’s battalion ended up the hardest hit Marine unit of the entire Iraq war, and he lost some of his best friends over there.
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-mar26.8i0KMo&refcode=em260328-1-90&refcode2=4102.734936.iJbxNK&t=6&akid=4102%2E734936%2EiJbxNK)
---
After he came home he had to fight just as hard to get the health care, services, and benefits he and his brothers earned in combat. He knew the system was broken, and was determined to fix it. So, he ran for Congress — and won.
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-mar26.8i0KMo&refcode=em260328-1-90&refcode2=4102.734936.iJbxNK&t=7&akid=4102%2E734936%2EiJbxNK)
---
Then, on January 6th, everything changed. He was ready to fight for his country again, but this time on the floor of the House of Representatives. It wasn’t just about improving things anymore — it was about defending our democracy itself.
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-mar26.8i0KMo&refcode=em260328-1-90&refcode2=4102.734936.iJbxNK&t=8&akid=4102%2E734936%2EiJbxNK)
---
So, he ran for Senate. He took on one of Trump’s most devoted loyalists. It was one of the hardest fought and expensive elections in the country, but Ruben won.
[](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-mar26.8i0KMo&refcode=em260328-1-90&refcode2=4102.734936.iJbxNK&t=9&akid=4102%2E734936%2EiJbxNK)
---
Ruben never would’ve guessed this is how things were going to turn out.
But he’s learned a thing or two since he was that kid sleeping on the floor of the apartment. He learned that it isn’t the rich and powerful who suffer when our leaders fail. It's people like his mom, his Marines, his teachers who lose when guys like Trump run the show.
He’s also learned a thing or two about winning tough races. We need to win everywhere this year — especially in purple and red states — and nobody’s better positioned to help than Ruben. But none of that work comes cheap.
[**So, we’re humbly asking if you can make a $5 donation to Ruben’s campaign before the first, official FEC deadline of the year hits at midnight on March 31st. He can’t do this alone.**](https://act.gallegoforarizona.com/go/1000?c0=ruben-em-mar26.8i0KMo&refcode=em260328-1-90&t=10&akid=4102%2E734936%2EiJbxNK)

St. Louis County is facing millions in debt-- and a significant increase from the $40 million deficit three years ago. Despite this, wasteful spending continues while essential services suffer:

* Animal Welfare: The state previously declined to accredit the St. Louis County animal shelter due to overcrowding, poor sanitation, and disrepair.
* Public Safety and Oversight: Lack of Council oversight has resulted in multiple inmate deaths in the County jail over the last eight years.
* Accountability: The auditor's office has consistently failed to perform its primary function.
* Fiscal Mismanagement: Millions have been wasted on ill-conceived projects, including a $3.2 million "farming collective" on contaminated land and $520,000 on a failed measure that threatened the separation of powers. My priority is to restore a balanced budget so we can focus on the most vulnerable members of our community. My platform includes:

* Neighborhood Improvement: I will take decisive action against illegal dumping to clean up our streets and tributaries.
* Healthcare Access: I am committed to protecting and expanding healthcare services through the St. Louis County Department of Health, especially for those at risk of losing health insurance coverage under the Affordable Care Act (ACA) and Medicaid.
* Public Health Expertise: As your State Senator, I held 100 town hall meetings and interviewed over 1,700 victims of nuclear contamination. I will bring this unparalleled research and expertise to the Council to address radioactive waste exposure throughout St. Louis County.
* Justice for Victims: I will hold the prosecutor's office accountable to ensure unsolved murders are investigated and victims receive justice.
* Principled Leadership: I will provide a strong, independent voice for the 1st District and will not compromise our community's interests for partisan politics. I believe in timely constituent services and professional leadership. I am running to bring accountability and results back to St. Louis County.

Despite this, wasteful spending continues while essential services suffer: Animal Welfare: The state previously declined to accredit the St. Louis County animal shelter due to overcrowding, poor sanitation, and disrepair. Public Safety and Oversight: Lack of Council oversight has resulted in multiple inmate deaths in the County jail over the last eight years. Accountability: The auditor's office has consistently failed to perform its primary function. Fiscal Mismanagement: Millions have been wasted on ill-conceived projects, including a $3.2 million "farming collective" on contaminated land and $520,000 on a failed measure that threatened the separation of powers. My priority is to restore a balanced budget so we can focus on the most vulnerable members of our community. My platform includes: Neighborhood Improvement: I will take decisive action against illegal dumping to clean up our streets and tributaries. Healthcare Access: I am committed to protecting and expanding healthcare services through the St. Louis County Department of Health, especially for those at risk of losing health insurance coverage under the Affordable Care Act (ACA) and Medicaid. Public Health Expertise: As your State Senator, I held 100 town hall meetings and interviewed over 1,700 victims of nuclear contamination. I will bring this unparalleled research and expertise to the Council to address radioactive waste exposure throughout St. Louis County. Justice for Victims: I will hold the prosecutor's office accountable to ensure unsolved murders are investigated and victims receive justice. Principled Leadership: I will provide a strong, independent voice for the 1st District and will not compromise our community's interests for partisan politics. I believe in timely constituent services and professional leadership. I am running to bring accountability and results back to St. Louis County. As a former state senator, I know the commitment, critical thinking and energy it takes to do exceptional work on behalf of taxpayers. ~ ** I am asking for your financial support so we can have a competitive race in District 1. ~ ~ ~ ~ | ~ ~ ~ You've been such a great support system in the past, and I need you now more than ever. Together, we can do this! Thank you in advance, Maria Chappelle-Nadal For By Chappelle-Nadal For County Council. Maria Chappelle-Nadal, Treasurer. P.O. Box 300024 University City, MO 63130 |

> For far too long, a bureaucratic deep state has operated on American soil with impunity, and escaped accountability from we the people. Recently declassified documents by the Director of National Intelligence (DNI) Tulsi Gabbard shows just how far the Obama administration and its lackeys were willing to go to keep an outsider like, then candidate Donald Trump from ever seeing the inside of the White House.
> [Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.AcCMc1w7Gf0ZpzpgpjBZL0fpcn-ff1wGkare_VU4PGI?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=192548614)
> We're talking about documents that expose blatant misconduct at the highest levels of government by Barrack Obama's administration; revealing how top officials like, John Brennan, James Comey, and John Clapper orchestrated a scheme to undermine the presidency of then President Elect Donald Trump. This isn't just a scandal; it's our worst fears realized and deserves every ounce of our outrage. It's an absolute disgrace and must be brought forward to see the light of day.
>
> Director Gabbard is not just handing us pieces of paper, she's throwing down the gauntlet. She's demanding that we confront the ugly truth regarding the lengths the bureaucratic deep state was willing to go to preserve their power. They symbolize the arrogance and hubris of an elite class that believes it is above reproach and can escape accountability, while trampling over the rights of everyday Americans.
>
> These documents scream that our former intelligence agencies stooped to new lows, fabricating documents, providing false testimony, and falsifying FISA warrant applications to surveil Donald Trump, and his associates based on the dubious and discredited "Steele dossier;" commonly known as the "Russia collusion hoax." Folks, this isn't just politics as usual, it's an unprecedented assault on our democracy itself.
>
> Foreign Intelligence Surveillance (FISA) warrants, the so-called judicial oversight mechanism meant to protect citizens from overreach, were turned into weapons in the hands of these reprobates. With false information derived from the fabricated Steele dossier, which was procured and funded by Hilary Clinton's campaign, they managed to spy on a United States Presidential candidate.
>
> How's that for election integrity? You'd think that the people tasked with safeguarding our nation would behave with some semblance of integrity, but no, they chose to pick a side and corrupted the very system they swore to protect.
>
> But why, why would they conduct themselves in such an egregious manner? The answer is quite simple, fear. Fear that a political outsider might actually disrupt their long-standing systemic corruption. They could not trust a man that wasn't beholden to the system. So, instead of welcoming honest political discourse, they opted for intimidation, deceit, and manipulation, while the fake news media parroted their narrative. The term "fake news media" is a well-deserved term; and let's not ever forget their complicity in this matter. They were all too eager to pounce on Trump's every misstep and provide cover for the rogue deep state operatives.
>
> So here we are with undeniable evidence that points to a coordinated effort to undermine Trump's candidacy, and ultimately his presidency. Unfortunately, more often than not, these career bureaucrats get to walk away without substantial consequences; but that ends now. The time has come for the abusers of the public trust to be brought to light and face substantial scrutiny; no matter who they are.
>
> We the people must understand the enormity of this situation. The malfeasance designed to subvert America's electoral process cannot go unpunished. We must hold these high-ranking wrongdoers accountable. We cannot be ok with our intelligence agencies playing political hit-squad, and then going on a book tour to pontificate their moral superiority. Because if we are, we can say goodbye to integrity in America's elections forever.
>
> Tulsi Gabbard has placed the ball squarely in the people's court, and it's up to the people to demand answers. Will we allow the deep-state elitists to trample on our way of life, or will we stand up for the democratic principles our republic was founded upon? I will say this, if we continue to sit idly by, we will deserve exactly what we get. When all is said and done, President Obama and his security cabinet manufactured and politicized intelligence to lay the groundwork for what was essentially a years-long coup. Let that sink all the way in.

body:
When parental rights meet the courts: A new RMV investigation into a case unfolding in Garfield County
| | | | [](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
---
**March 29, 2026** **SUNDAY NEWS DIGEST**
| | Dear Rocky Mountain Voice family,
This week, we published one of the most important investigations we’ve done to date—and one that’s already striking a chord across Colorado.

It starts with a single family in Garfield County.

But it raises much bigger questions about parental rights, the role of schools and outside advocates, and what happens when family disputes move into the courtroom.

In [Part 1 of our investigation](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.), we follow the story of Heather Fitzke, a mother of six who says her family’s situation didn’t begin in a courtroom—but that’s where everything changed. Within days, what began as a breakdown in communication turned into an emergency guardianship case that ultimately removed decision-making authority from her as a parent.

According to court filings, that shift happened quickly.

After being reported as a runaway, Fitzke’s child attempted to re-enroll in school. Days later, [a petition for emergency guardianship was filed by another adult](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)—and granted by a judge the very next day, transferring authority over schooling, medical care and daily decisions.

What followed was a series of hearings, restraining orders, and legal battles that left the family separated—and still dealing with the fallout months later.

But [Part 2 of the investigation](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) reveals what shaped that outcome.

Court records show the case relied heavily on letters, testimony, and screenshots, including statements from other parents, social media posts, and text messages attributed to Fitzke.

Those materials painted a picture of a parent accused of creating an unsafe environment, while Fitzke maintains her words and actions were misrepresented in the process.

At the same time, her public comments at a local school board meeting—where she raised concerns about [gender identity policies and parental notification](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)—were later cited in filings, sometimes in ways she says did not match what she actually said.

The case also unfolded amid broader community tensions over school policies, activism, and parental rights—where individuals involved in those debates later appeared in court filings connected to the case.

And as the legal process moved forward, restrictions were placed not just on custody—but on communication.

An [amended protection order limited Fitzke’s contact with her child](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) and even restricted what she could say publicly about the case.

Today, the impact is still being felt. A family separated. Tens of thousands of dollars in legal costs. And a case that, depending on who you ask, represents either a necessary intervention—or a system that moved too quickly, with consequences that can’t easily be undone.

This isn't just about one family. It’s about [how quickly authority can shift](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)—from parents, to schools, to courts. It’s about how allegations, advocacy, and public narratives [intersect inside the legal system](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.).

We encourage you to read both parts of this investigation carefully and come to your own conclusions. Where should the line between parental rights and institutional authority be drawn?

**Read Part 1 and Part 2 here:**
1️⃣ [How a Garfield County dispute turned into a court-ordered separation](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)
2️⃣ [The record that removed a child: Allegations, filings and fallout](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)

In truth & liberty, Team RMV

| | **TOP STORIES OF THE WEEK**
---
**[From party switch to $6.4 million: Examining the rise of a CD4 candidate](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)**
**[](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.)** BY SHAINA COLE, [ROCKY MOUNTAIN VOICE](https://link.email.rockymountainvoice.) In a matter of months, Eileen Laubacher went from a newly registered Democrat with no primary voting history to the best-funded candidate in Colorado’s 4th Congressional District. **_How are you standing up to the President?_**
While President Trump has broken promise after promise to the American people, we’ve been fighting back.
When the president and MAGA Republicans attempted to sell off our public lands last summer, we fought back and won.
We helped take the president's illegal tariff-taxes to court. The Supreme Court struck them down and now we’re demanding that President Trump pays you back.
And we’re rejecting President Trump’s plea to send $200 billion to his illegal war in Iran, fighting to safeguard affordable health care, and refusing to bend to the president’s will when he attacks Colorado.
**_Why is your race so important?_**
This is a big one, and the answer is pretty simple: There’s NO PATH for Democrats to flip the Senate blue without defending this seat in Colorado.
That means if we want to win back our power in Washington and bring Trump’s disastrous agenda to a screeching halt, we have to protect this seat.
MAGA knows this, too. That’s why they’ve made Colorado one of their top targets this year. They’re gearing up to do – and spend – whatever it takes to flip this seat back to red.
**_How can I help?_**
By reading emails like this one, staying focused on the work ahead, organizing your community, and even chipping in if you can!
Look, running for Senate is outrageously expensive — especially in a critical swing seat like this one. We don’t take a penny from corporate PACs, so to hold the line here, we’re relying on folks like you.

| Dear Friend,
A moment that stopped me cold wasn't the woman handing out cash. It wasn't the homeless man who had no idea what he was signing. It wasn't even the petitioner who followed my producer down the street threatening to **"knock him out."** It was the cop. Officer Maraveilla of the LAPD was sitting right there — **feet away from 28 documented instances of federal election fraud** — watching people exchange cash for voter registrations in broad daylight. And when we asked him about it, here's what he said: **"I mean, if it's nonprofit... they're signing it. It's consensual. It's more of a civil thing — like they're not telling them no."** That's the officer assigned to Skid Row every single day. He doesn't know the California law. He doesn't know the federal statute. He watched a federal felony happen in front of him and called it a contractual dispute. **[**This is why we exist.**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom. In 2019, **nine individuals were prosecuted by the Los Angeles DA for this exact crime** — exchanging cigarettes and cash for petition signatures. Fourteen counts. Same California Elections Code §18603. Same Skid Row. But here's the critical difference: **none of it was on video.** Not one second of footage. It was word against word, and the prosecutions went nowhere that mattered. This time, we have everything on tape. We have **28 documented exchanges on hidden camera**. We have Brenda Brown's face. We have her saying, **"I'm paying you guys. I need to get paid too."** We have the petitioner's pyramid scheme explained in their own words. We have the Weingart Center employee directing our journalist to where the fraud was happening. We have the LASA worker who falsely identified himself as LAPD to try to stop us. When our undercover journalist kept asking questions, one of the petitioners followed him and threatened — on camera — to **"move him down the street,"** then: **"I'll knock you out looking right at me. Don't come over here again. I'mma beat your ass."** He didn't back down. He stayed in the field. He got the footage. **That kind of courage doesn't come cheap, and it doesn't happen without your financial support.** [****](https://link.email.america1stwarroom. Many thanks to Team Beth Farnham for Congress who assembled signs last Saturday! Pictured are Team Members: Maribeth Fish, Sandra Hartzell, and Brian Ecker, and bonus volunteers Shannon Jackson, Deb Martinez, and Laura Anderson. Because of their efforts, I was able to deliver over 75 signs around the district as I participated in events. And this week I ordered 1000 signs that have a new design!

Together, we [#ChooseDemocracy](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=242713714fdd8e154ef6118cff2b471dea2abc6fec301aa38912f735a28be29d&blog_id=213069660&post_id=6681&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=8e60c4b2cac5b2ee61a7ed47623eca54&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_&email_id=2fe980b408e1196bd040a434e1eb4b2a) !
---
| **Americans suffer, Enemies plunder, under Trump**
---
| |
---
In a variety of ways, Trump’s incompetence from his emotional tariff-by-tweet policy to his illegally-declared war in Iran to his lifting of Iranian sanctions, is costing Americans at home while our identified “enemies” of Russia and Iran are making out like bandits.
---
For Americans, the cost of gas, groceries, fertilizer, and energy have increased substantially, especially with the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Additionally, the weapons used in Iran are costing hundreds of millions, if not billions, per day. These will cost Americans more tax dollars or reduced food assistance, healthcare, and other benefits in the near future.
---
Meanwhile, to ease the price of gasoline, Trump lifted sanctions against Iran (the very country he choose to create a war against!) leading to them receiving $14Billion.
---
And with the blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, Russia becomes the main supplier of fertilizer, creating a booming economy in this area for them.
---
Check out the corresponding articles:
---
[https://www.thenation.com/article/economy/us-affordability-crisis-inflation-trump-economy-inequality/](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=440f895aa6ba54d69b0653cf6e6d98c935696c07018861e7403584f444625bdd&blog_id=213069660&post_id=6681&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=8cb26a7e3a3c5c2da45d17f74628714d&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cudGhlbmF0aW9uLmNvbS9hcnRpY2xlL2Vjb25vbXkvdXMtYWZmb3JkYWJpbGl0eS1jcmlzaXMtaW5mbGF0aW9uLXRydW1wLWVjb25vbXktaW5lcXVhbGl0eS8&email_id=2fe980b408e1196bd040a434e1eb4b2a)
“Farmers were already contending with high costs and plummeting sales thanks to Trump’s [unprovoked trade war](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=d3391bcb9165d9ff6b74f5a90bc4b9419ec9579ca9746fa7e8e91e245ef696c1&blog_id=213069660&post_id=6681&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=801c59ed7ae9c048bc4add4e3832e3f3&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly9hcG5ld3MuY29tL2FydGljbGUvdHJ1bXAtc295YmVhbi1mYXJtZXJzLWNoaW5hLXRyYWRlLXRhcmlmZnMtYnJhemlsLTk2NjM3NTlhYzNjOWM3MzYwYmQ1ZjIzY2I4NDE4MGYw&email_id=2fe980b408e1196bd040a434e1eb4b2a) with China. Now that he’s instigated an [actual war with Iran](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=fcf68cfedf2a4ac19efa527692be4980c0a7d1cd976cce1ddd4effce8135b403&blog_id=213069660&post_id=6681&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=636b29774dea07ab6d10e5878efd892e&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_url=aHR0cHM6Ly9hcG5ld3MuY29tL2FydGljbGUvaXJhbi13YXItZmVydGlsaXplci1hdmFpbGFiaWxpdHktY29zdC1mYXJtZXJzLWFhODQ2ZmIwZTMwZDEwNjBkODk5M2M2NWQzMmZlMTJi&email_id=2fe980b408e1196bd040a434e1eb4b2a), prices for fuel and fertilizer are sharply rising, too, with the potential to set off a cascade of inflation that spreads from the cost of feed to prices at the butcher counter. | **No AI Data Centers in Franklin County!**
---
| | |
---|---|---
On Thursday, I attended the Franklin County Farm Bureau meeting, where Tom Beresnyak of the Penn State Extension presented on AI data centers. This was an opportunity for our farmers to understand the impact of AI data centers should they sell their farmland for this purpose.
---
My takeaway?
---
AI data centers definitely don’t belong in Franklin County.
---
It’s not that I don’t believe in the application of AI, but it should be very strategic in its implementation.
---
Unfortunately, lately, it has been used for propaganda. Indeed, the first example of AI generated content that Mr. Beresnyak shared was a video of an acquaintance driving a racecar. Honestly, if he hadn’t announced that it was AI generated, I would have believed the video to be real. And therein lies the danger. AI content should never be mistaken for actual human created content.
---
And though I can’t deny the “gee whiz” factor of it all I feel strongly that students especially don’t need it so much either.
---
Beresnyak did attempt to justify it through slides on some real and hypothetical help that federal and state departments of agriculture posited it could provide, but then he shifted his presentation to justifying data centers in general. Yes, we need data centers for storing financial and medical information, streaming videos and posting on Facebook, but those are, ahem, HUMAN GENERATED CONTENT. Real filmmakers have messages they want to impart to audiences. Real people want to connect with other real people through social media. Justifying data centers still doesn’t justify AI DATA CENTERS.
---
Further into the presentation, he spoke about power and water usage. I learned that a lot of AI data centers want to build near the infrastructure of natural gas because of its capacity. Fortunately, or unfortunately, Franklin County is not located within the natural gas basin, and therefore we would have to rely on nuclear power to generate the consistent power AI data centers need.
---
Many arguments are made against AI data centers for their water usage, but this was parsed very well in the presentation. If the AI data centers use wet cooling, that is the evaporative water, then, yes, too much water is used by the data centers, but if they used dry cooling or closed loop, think a radiator, then the draw upon the water is not as great, so there may be less draw upon water resources in the future as they perfect the closed loop systems.
---
However, whatever points he gained through the possibility of water mitigation, he quickly forfeited. Tom presented the creation of jobs – that high skilled labor was needed, especially plumbers or Tech Engineers – but then he joked that AI data centers are built with fake Windows because there really isn’t anyone in them.
---
In other words , he validated what I heard AI data centers provide – construction jobs, but not truly permanent jobs. So, that’s a real concern for the long-term investment in the community.
---
Lastly, he didn’t seem to know how much space, power, and water Penn State’s own AI system, Tilva, uses though he made a point to sing its virtues. He’ll get back to us on that.
---
All in all, it was an interesting exercise to see how those steeped in the dreams of Elon Musk sell them to others and I was grateful to attend.
---
Together, we [#ChooseDemocracy](http://bethfarnhamforcongress.com?action=user_content_redirect&uuid=a358d4796dd5b09f5ba5201fcc93c5594490039f07a161422e7ad0f0b6278da0&blog_id=213069660&post_id=6681&user_id=248418217&subs_id=487468588&signature=7ce012ef53a41e44b1d8ae064f6661e7&email_name=new-post&user_email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&encoded_&email_id=2fe980b408e1196bd040a434e1eb4b2a) !

name: Tim Walz
subject: What I saw yesterday
disclaimer_text: paid for by Walz for Governor
body:
#
Peter,
What I saw yesterday at the No Kings rally in Minnesota was bigger than one event, one crowd, or one moment. It was a reminder of who we are as Minnesotans and Americans.
When a wannabe dictator in the White House tried to bully, intimidate, and divide people, Minnesotans stood together.
We stood up for our neighbors. We stood up for decency. We stood up for kindness. And yesterday, at a moment when democracy itself feels at risk, Minnesota did it again.
**Thousands showed up, stood together, and made it clear that fear is not going to define this state, and it is not going to define this country.**
The work ahead is not small. But if yesterday proved anything, it is that people are ready to meet this moment — with courage, with conviction, and with each other.
With hope,
— Tim Walz

Email us: [info@walzforgovernor.org](mailto:info@walzforgovernor.org)
This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com. Email is the most important way we keep in touch with people like you, so thank you for reading to the end.

Sustainer Sunday is back
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260329-2665)
Peter,
Hope everyone had a wonderful weekend! For this week's edition of Sustainer Sunday, we're bringing you a story from a student activist.
Meet Noah Dinan, a student at the Milwaukee School of Engineering:
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260329.-NhhUb&refcode=em20260329-2665&t=1&akid=2665%2E105371%2EuS5NQ0)
* * *
_I got into organizing when a group came to MSOE's campus targeting LGBTQ+ students. Several of us organized a counter-protest — I couldn't just stand by. Afterward, I met students flying a YDSA flag and started learning about the chapter. I've been attending meetings and volunteering ever since._
_We've been fighting to get ICE off campus and improve life for students. But activism for me is bigger than any single issue — it's about promoting working class and investing in community power, protecting trans folks and LGBTQ+ communities, ending the wars our government is waging. Kindness to all. That's what drives me._
_When I saw Fran fighting for the same things — and saw that DSA endorsed her — I became an instant volunteer and supporter. She's actually in the fight._
_To anyone who's skeptical about Fran or undecided in their choice for governor: Ignore terms like 'democratic socialist' and look at what policy candidates are actually fighting for. Ask yourself if those things align with your values._
\- Noah Dinan, Milwaukee
* * *
We are so grateful for Noah and everything he's done to spread the word on campus and activate the student community. Earning the support of young people whose futures are at stake is the ultimate vote of confidence.
But we're still fighting an uphill battle on fundraising. This movement doesn't run on PAC money or corporate donors. It runs on people like Noah giving what they can.

Team Hong

On April 21, Virginians will vote on a constitutional amendment that ensures voters — not politicians — have the final say on congressional maps before the midterm elections.
**Across the country, Donald Trump and MAGA Republicans are coordinating an unprecedented power grab to rig the midterm elections. They’ve already manipulated maps in states like Texas and North Carolina — and they’re trying to do it in Florida right now.**
**Virginia has the chance to fight back.**

What I saw at 3 No Kings rallies | | [ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMYE5U9NTRbOMLNsSMiwuHsSrn4JnyYtk1EREaCYHldIw2Es-lCsKe-k7RYeRErCjUmpL6YWg0aqprxBCSlqaUKjL6uf8EDq6vQVEaFZEFWaTvOKtPnFc2PEalY2SnM4_7SSYi6VY4knapQ7FFJ8M9SV-tdvBYYalEXqzNaQiT7ZAKq5daFurUl1kHGa2YID82O3C2A0m93KsKiXJN4tVi_nfwnGZAPO4mbQrnOog2jlx0ex_NkZu6DCZF-rGvq8JWAOJyDGm9rWSRhILfUU5ofU/4pc/ZOxqg2BNSQeGR1NmL_QS6A/h0/h001.EfnWxPDNFUoZ8PQFAfzw2TMLjpuLfI-_tgd1qN7VYBk)

Peter, Yesterday I stood with my neighbors in Greenville, McKinney, and Farmersville at three No Kings protests across TX-03. I saw teachers and veterans and small business owners and young families standing together because they believe the same thing our founders believed when they sat down to write the Declaration of Independence: **No one gets to be a king in America.**
---
[ **NO KINGS IN TX-03** ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt84a3q63BDVi2ahj-hHZOqnEslk_DjJ2O582St1Dz0ka9YwcNLDiDXVn7NE_NB3_rLxeQTqt6CEFfFIFuZgRQlj5Ih8B0wyUm2ACukTT74wTPGla4LXq4cNkgSaXZnciG8cY7MPTUJr8nhD5iwqtR4qpTsMno57_OA4eo72QHVLN6_mB6v60vTs23SOr8LE-LglApKnLBBuZhy7mQ5cNzrUEWiM8cMRhoKDdnrS8goLtyHBMDYUi6sw9eLbaH6oemqgE0j-tInngHtchVVS9EJFnXRhUf8pFGiAjMm4yKKIZpBK7pwvkTXJYXhwuH4kWkSg/4pc/ZOxqg2BNSQeGR1NmL_QS6A/h1/h001.wc6DneIV6AJR0-TdTEgC-_gfNmIHERnO5FpKtSDoXPw)

Robert Kennedy put it best in 1966.
“Each time a person stands up for an ideal, or acts to improve the lot of others, or strikes out against injustice, they send forth a tiny ripple of hope. Crossing each other from a million different centers of energy and daring, those ripples build a current that can sweep down the mightiest walls of oppression and resistance.”
Yesterday I watched those ripples move through three Texas communities and I felt every one of them.
[Help us turn those ripples into a wave that flips this seat in November.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt84a3q63BDVi2ahj-hHZOqnEslk_DjJ2O582St1Dz0ka9cPMxCFvuTnC0oLUYqXh5qyfOl8TTqr65XX6rv5cmE-pLTfiTBQRk-wTOWHEU6ehamrK-FF4z6gFH_0TTKADJuivj7wJ2bqwoVG9nYkKa7SFRgubX19tkAJv8gBh8MzfuD6c_rOK76SQnAAkwUFkqsqgFBtECyolJr0BVvWh_O34aQw9QgkgprYXzBLz3csEamUHTR8SIUe2wzgWgb8UJ4m-Z7T9ookqSJutAPldkbzEW9cnJWGF7zIeBjnPQmERka54tNjWle3BxyodCZBEvAw/4pc/ZOxqg2BNSQeGR1NmL_QS6A/h2/h001.ZZsnawtbLCnEv4np4KMyaoTE_yftTsbUdamEoBkH1xk)

When our founders declared independence they also listed specific abuses of power so that future generations would recognize tyranny. King George refused laws for the public good. He controlled the judges. He kept standing armies without consent. And he taxed without representation, ignoring elected bodies that challenged his power in the 13 Colonies. They wrote it all down because they knew someday someone would need the list. Right now we have a president who describes political opponents as enemies and demands personal loyalty from institutions designed to be independent. He claims broad immunity from accountability and uses the language of violence against those who dissent. Our founders laid down those principles in the full knowledge that they were signing their own death warrants if they failed, and Trump is testing those boundaries without a moment of that same courage or consequence. **Keith Self has watched every one of those tests and celebrated each move towards tyranny. ** The people I stood with yesterday in Greenville, McKinney, and Farmersville have not made that choice. They showed up because they understand that the work of forming a more perfect union belongs to all of us and it never stops. [**Help us take that energy all the way to November and remind Keith Self and this administration that there are no kings in America.**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt84a3q63BDVi2ahj-hHZOqnEslk_DjJ2O582St1Dz0ka96piA_XEoJ1-q_ckIFPg2IekFWBMVeAVa_LXwPo6ykKOrGMPf2PmNblUW50H3bmiIRIhCxtUbDW4eRpo_wqLV9zW-fC4gA3aV59TeriO2vwsTUSKKqEwn8ac-c-s_lqOzGT0nm-B1EQlhsp6ko_iSd6QpgHJ9znuf5k_81VzXkwiUx5_l4uMHN4B3bg7IBKvQkJBizknYNyN9hPbuSgqO0b99Zha3x8YcT4McEEfZ4kvV_0GGTsUv2c0Zl9zzrTUeD1iE2o3jo-qqqc4mWj0UTA/4pc/ZOxqg2BNSQeGR1NmL_QS6A/h4/h001.0DyDvc9jp6yvSNefXcj6aJ4QjlwNmPXLnElEzjEIFbM) Very respectfully, Evan Hunt Democratic Nominee TX-03

clean_body: What I saw at 3 No Kings rallies | | Peter, Yesterday I stood with my neighbors in Greenville, McKinney, and Farmersville at three No Kings protests across TX-03. I saw teachers and veterans and small business owners and young families standing together because they believe the same thing our founders believed when they sat down to write the Declaration of Independence: No one gets to be a king in America. Robert Kennedy put it best in 1966. “Each time a person stands up for an ideal, or acts to improve the lot of others, or strikes out against injustice, they send forth a tiny ripple of hope. Crossing each other from a million different centers of energy and daring, those ripples build a current that can sweep down the mightiest walls of oppression and resistance.” Yesterday I watched those ripples move through three Texas communities and I felt every one of them. | When our founders declared independence they also listed specific abuses of power so that future generations would recognize tyranny. King George refused laws for the public good. He controlled the judges. He kept standing armies without consent. And he taxed without representation, ignoring elected bodies that challenged his power in the 13 Colonies. They wrote it all down because they knew someday someone would need the list. Right now we have a president who describes political opponents as enemies and demands personal loyalty from institutions designed to be independent. He claims broad immunity from accountability and uses the language of violence against those who dissent. Our founders laid down those principles in the full knowledge that they were signing their own death warrants if they failed, and Trump is testing those boundaries without a moment of that same courage or consequence. Keith Self has watched every one of those tests and celebrated each move towards tyranny. The people I stood with yesterday in Greenville, McKinney, and Farmersville have not made that choice. They showed up because they understand that the work of forming a more perfect union belongs to all of us and it never stops. Very respectfully, Evan Hunt Democratic Nominee TX-03 | | | Evan Hunt is a combat aviator and veteran, a community and business leader, and a Texas family man, running against MAGA Rep. clean_body: Everything costs more, and everyone knows it | | Matt Maasdam is a husband, a father, and a Navy SEAL. He carried the nuclear football for President Obama — now he's running as a Democrat to flip Michigan's 7th congressional district. If you’d like to unsubscribe, | | Democracy only works with input from the people. That’s why I’ve made it a priority to speak with as many Michiganders as possible. Recently I got together with a group from Milford, South Lyon, Brighton, and Pinckney. The message is universal: everything costs more, and everyone knows it. A cashier at Busch's pointed out she doesn't need a report to tell her prices are too high — she hears it from people at the cash register every day. Yet, Tom Barrett seems to be deaf to the problems we’re facing. He’s overseeing the burning of taxpayer dollars on increasingly reckless endeavors. This is why it’s so important to have a representative who’s actually tapped in with their constituents. The problem is obvious. The least Congress can do is not exacerbate the problems by lazily allowing expensive tariffs and endless wars to continue. My Team and I are doing everything we can to hear as many voices as possible, but the fact is that this will be one of the most expensive Congressional campaigns in the country. If we could bankroll our outreach with a couple checks from a corporation, flipping MI-07 would be easy. | | | Hi Peter, I just stood up in front of thousands of Democrats at Pueblo Memorial Hall and poured my heart out about why I love democracy. Not as an abstract idea, but as a set of choices we make together about what kind of Colorado we're going to be. **The feelings right now are real big**. **Today we earned 63.1% of the vote at state assembly** , which means we're officially on the ballot for the Democratic primary! Not only that, but because we earned the largest percentage of the vote, we’ll be listed first on the ballot–an honor known as “top lining!” We couldn’t have done it without you. If you're thinking, "Wait, I thought you were already on the ballot," totally fair. Getting on the primary ballot is just the first step in any campaign, and state assembly is where a lot of that is decided. These election processes are complicated, which is exactly why Colorado needs an expert like me for Secretary of State—someone who knows this system inside and out. It’s taken so much work to get to this moment, and I'm so proud of the campaign that we've built—people-powered and grounded in real competence. **I'm grateful you're part of it.** Now comes the next chapter: **winning the primary on June****30,** so Colorado's elections are in safe hands heading into the next presidential cycle.**Here's how to keep us rolling:** If you can, chip in $10 or $25 to help us reach the Democrats who won't tune in until they're literally holding their ballot. # [Let me explain this FEC thing...](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6380051&post_id=192313788&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTkyMzEzNzg4LCJpYXQiOjE3NzQ4MjcyMDAsImV4cCI6MTc3NzQxOTIwMCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTYzODAwNTEiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.RtxhuEhoqncInUFizS6JJcjvXT4rzkAqBCBkDK7EpDg)
### Why an unsexy campaign deadline actually matters in a battleground race like Michigan.
| | [Haley Stevens](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---
| Mar 29
---
| [](https://substack.com/@haleyformi)
---

---
| | | [](https://substack..32ku6Sc9YuUT_Ie43NeenSn4r-q-CRtlXlKjqLkSGPM?&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email)
---
| | [READ IN APP](https://open.substack.com/pub/haleyformi/p/let-me-explain-this-fec-thing?utm_source=email&redirect=app-store&utm_campaign=email-read-in-app)
---

Hi friends,
You've probably heard me - or folks from my campaign - talking a lot lately about this upcoming FEC deadline.
And if you're like most people, your first reaction was probably not: "Wow! Cool! Please tell me more about federal campaign finance reporting!"
_I get it._
The FEC is not exactly a thrilling topic of conversation for most.
**But before you scroll away, hear me out: this FEC deadline really does matter.**
And because I'm a policy nerd who genuinely loves explaining how this stuff affects people in Michigan, I thought I'd take a minute to walk through what it is, why campaigns talk about it so much, and why it matters in a race like ours.
So crack open a pop, because class is in session. I promise this won't take long, and there's definitely no quiz.
The**Federal Election Commission** , or FEC, is a regulatory agency that requires campaigns to report how much money they raise and how many donations they receive every three months.
Those numbers become public. The idea is that everybody can see who is funding any given candidate, how strong their support is, and who truly has the resources to compete and win.
These numbers, especially in a battleground race like ours, are critical.
These are the numbers the national media sees. MAGA megadonors see them. And our supporters see them too.
**That 's why this deadline matters.**
It's not just some random filing date buried in a government spreadsheet somewhere. It's the first big public snapshot of this campaign in the election year.
And in a battleground race like ours, that snapshot says a lot.
And in Michigan, you better believe people are watching.
**Polling shows I 'm the strongest Democrat to take on Republican Mike Rogers. But the question everyone in politics starts asking at an FEC deadline is: [Does she have the resources to win?](https://substack.com/redirect/4bf8dc6e-7183-491e-b30a-e863e43b0290?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
That's why a strong FEC report sends a loud message.
It says the polls are right.
It says working people are paying attention.
It says Michigan is not for sale.
And it says this campaign has the resources to win.
When Republicans and their billionaire backers see weakness, they smell an opening. They spend more money. They flood the airwaves. They try to stop our momentum.
That's the part of campaigns nobody loves, but it's real.
**[So when my team talks about an FEC deadline, what we're really talking about is whether we can publicly show the strength behind what we're building together.](https://substack.com/redirect/4bf8dc6e-7183-491e-b30a-e863e43b0290?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
And honestly, I'm so proud of what we're building. Because this campaign is not powered by some MAGA oil billionaire from Texas.
It's powered by working people.
By teachers. Nurses. Autoworkers. Small-business owners. Hardworking parents trying to make ends meet. People who are sick and tired of being left behind. People who are ready to fight back.
That matters to me. _A lot._
These are my people.
Because I've always believed the true strength of a campaign is not whether one wealthy person can write a huge check. It's whether thousands of regular people are willing to step up and say: _heck yes, I 'm in. I believe in this. I want to be part of it._
So yes, it's a filing deadline. But it's also a public measure of momentum, energy, and the people-powered strength we need to win.
**[If you're in a position to chip in before this FEC deadline, I'd be grateful. Truly. Even a few dollars helps us show the strength of this grassroots campaign and keep building what we know Michigan needs.](https://substack.com/redirect/4bf8dc6e-7183-491e-b30a-e863e43b0290?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/4bf8dc6e-7183-491e-b30a-e863e43b0290?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thanks for letting me nerd out on campaign mechanics for a minute.
I'm so glad we're in this together.
With grit and gratitude,
Haley
* * *

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/4bf8dc6e-7183-491e-b30a-e863e43b0290?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football’s 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

In 1998, Coach Tuberville was announced as the next head coach for the Auburn Tigers. Tuberville’s time at Auburn was a success by any measure, as the Tigers captured eight consecutive bowl appearances, including five New Year’s Day bowl appearances, five SEC Western Division titles, one SEC Championship, and a 13-0 season in 2004, after which Coach Tuberville was once again named the AP’s SEC Coach of the Year. For his efforts during the perfect 2004 season, Tuberville would be named Paul “Bear” Bryant Coach of the Year, Associated Press Coach of the Year, Walter Camp Coach of the Year, Sporting News Coach of the Year, and AFCA Coach of the Year, among others.

_In 2020, Coach Tuberville became Senator Tuberville, winning his election to represent all Alabamians in the United States Senate with the full support of President Trump. Since then, he's supported President Trump's America-First policies while fighting off the Radical Left. clean_body: We saw a lot this week | 650 miles. That’s how many miles we racked up this week going out on the campaign trail, and I want to tell you about what we saw: We saw gas stations with prices going through the roof, thanks to MAGA’s unquestioning support of Trump’s illegal wars – which my Republican opponent supports wholeheartedly. We spoke with hardworking Wisconsinites about how to make Wisconsin a union state again. We talked with families about how our public schools are facing a funding crisis, and how the Washington Way is making it hard for Wisconsinites to raise their children here. As we spoke with folks from all walks of life on the campaign trail, I heard the same thing over and over again: Wisconsinites are barely scraping by while big corporations are raking in record profits. Wisconsin is a state full of promise – but we are also a state that is hurting. While the people I met have different stories and struggles, what they have in common is that their needs have been completely ignored by the MAGA agenda. We need change here in Wisconsin, and Donald Trump’s hand-picked candidate Tom Tiffany will just be a rubber stamp for business as usual. But with our end-of-quarter fundraising deadline in just 2 days, it is more important than ever to show the strength of our grassroots movement.
